articles.title: Atleta que perdeu movimento após golpe proibido no jiu-jitsu relata rotina de recuperação: 'É um dia de cada vez' | G1
articles.standfirst: Depois de passar semanas internado, o lutador Willian 'Kabuto' Hiroyuki voltou para casa, que precisou ser adaptada às novas necessidades. Em entrevista exclusiva ao Fantástico, ele falou sobre sua recuperação.
articles.summary: Depois de passar semanas internado, o lutador Willian 'Kabuto' Hiroyuki voltou para casa, que precisou ser adaptada às novas necessidades. Em entrevista exclusiva ao Fantástico, ele falou sobre sua recuperação.
articles.body:
O lutador Willian "Kabuto" Hiroyuki deu uma entrevista exclusiva ao Fantástico sobre sua recuperação desde que foi vítima de um golpe desleal durante uma luta de jiu-jitsu em Londrina, no Norte do Paraná.

Depois de passar semanas internado, o lutador voltou para casa, que precisou ser adaptada às novas necessidades. A rotina agora inclui fisioterapia e cuidados de profissionais de saúde.

“Antes de eu poder deslizar por baixo, do nada, eu apaguei”, relembrou. “Quando vi, eu estava com o meu corpo jogado no chão, sem poder mexer nada do corpo.”

Kabuto sofreu a lesão em 22 de agosto, durante uma disputa na categoria absoluto, que permite confrontos entre atletas de pesos diferentes.

O impacto provocou uma luxação entre a quinta e a sexta vértebras cervicais, com compressão do canal medular e lesão grave na medula. Como consequência, ele teve perda de força dos movimentos, especialmente das mãos e do pescoço para baixo.

"É um dia de cada vez. Mas não vou negar que tem dias que são difíceis", afirmou Kabuto.

O vídeo da luta viralizou e chegou ao promotor Renato Castro, que também é praticante de jiu-jitsu. "Imediatamente eu disse: 'com certeza esse comportamento é criminoso'". Ele noticiou os fatos à polícia, que deu início às investigações sobre o caso.

"Até o momento ouvimos 10 testemunhas. À exceção de uma, todas elas falaram que o golpe praticado que gerou essa lesão foi um golpe proibido na luta de jiu-jitsu", disse o delegado Roberto Fernandes. "Ele correu o risco de praticar uma lesão séria, o que a doutrina chama de dolo eventual".

O lutador William Kabuto — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

A organização garante que o torneio seguia todas as regras da Confederação Brasileira de Jiu-Jitsu (CBJJ) e que o árbitro agiu de acordo com o regulamento ao não parar o confronto quando Kabuto ainda estava suspenso, de cabeça para baixo.

"Ele não pode antecipar. Isso é da regra do esporte. Não tinha o que ele fazer. O que ele tinha que fazer, o que aconteceu aquilo, ele fez. Foi chamar a equipe de primeiros socorros ali pra fazer já os primeiros atendimentos com o William. E desclassificar o atleta", explica Cleber Takeuchi, organizador do campeonato.

Até esta reportagem, mais de um mês depois da luta, a CBJJ não havia se manifestado sobre o caso. Procurada pela equipe do Fantástico, a confederação afirmou que faz "a revisão contínua de suas regras, buscando preservar a integridade física e segurança dos atletas".

Depois da lesão, Kabuto manteve a consciência e se lembra da reação do adversário.

"Ele não falou nada, só olhou para mim e continuou olhando para o teto, sem nenhuma reação", diz Kabuto.

O advogado Felipe de Melo, que representa Juliano, disse que o lutador buscou contato com o professor de Kabuto. "Por excesso de cautela, ele resolveu esperar o melhor momento, mas desde o princípio se colocou à disposição para auxiliar no que fosse necessário", afirmou.

Juliano se pronunciou nas redes sociais logo após o campeonato. "Eu, no intuito de defender algo ali, botei o joelho pro chão e o cara tava embaixo de mim, eu não percebi. O cara muito magrinho, o cara acho que pesa uns 70 quilos. E pra evitar o desequilíbrio, eu joguei o joelho pro chão e o cara tava embaixo. E não deu tempo de fazer muita coisa", afirmou.

Não é a primeira vez que ele é investigado por agressão. Em 2016, Juliano foi condenado ao pagamento de danos morais por "dar um tapa no rosto e aplicar uma gravata" em uma mulher.

A casa da família já estava em reforma e precisou ser adaptada às novas necessidades. É ali, cercado pelos parentes e pelos profissionais que cuidam dele, que Kabuto começa uma etapa que ainda não tem previsão para terminar: a recuperação.

"Temos que ter esperança, porque ainda está muito cedo, muito precoce, e não podemos fechar nenhum prognóstico nesse momento", diz o médico.

"A primeira coisa é poder realmente ter a minha vida de volta, né?", afirma Kabuto.

articles.title: Influenciador Enaldinho contracena com Lázaro Ramos em edição especial do Criança Esperança | G1
articles.standfirst: O Criança Esperança 2026 vai ao ar nesta segunda-feira (12), depois da novela Quem Ama Cuida, na TV Globo.
articles.summary: O Criança Esperança 2026 vai ao ar nesta segunda-feira (12), depois da novela Quem Ama Cuida, na TV Globo.
articles.body:
O Criança Esperança deste ano terá uma participação inédita do influenciador Enaldinho, conhecido pelos vídeos de desafios e brincadeiras na internet. O especial será ambientado em uma biblioteca gigante, onde personagens da literatura ganham vida e histórias de diferentes gerações se encontram.

📅 O Criança Esperança 2026 vai ao ar nesta segunda-feira (12), depois da novela Quem Ama Cuida, na TV Globo.

Na atração, Enaldinho vai contracenar com Lázaro Ramos, que interpreta o guardião das histórias. O influenciador conta que sua entrada em cena será como se saísse de dentro de um livro. “A gente vai conversar sobre as brincadeiras de antigamente e as de hoje em dia, o que as crianças assistiam antigamente e o que assistem hoje em dia”, adiantou.

O especial reúne ainda nomes como Sandy, Michel Teló, Gaby Amarantos, Péricles e Gilberto Gil, que se apresenta ao lado da neta Flor Gil. Os artistas serão acompanhados pela Orquestra Sinfônica Brasileira, em um repertório que resgata músicas marcantes de diferentes gerações. Personagens como Emília e Cuca, do Sítio do Picapau Amarelo, também participam da atração.

articles.title: Coreia do Sul e Japão detectam lançamento de mísseis da Coreia do Norte em direção ao mar | G1
articles.standfirst: O lançamento dá continuidade a uma sequência recente de demonstrações de armamentos que aumentou as tensões em meio a um longo impasse diplomático.
articles.summary: O lançamento dá continuidade a uma sequência recente de demonstrações de armamentos que aumentou as tensões em meio a um longo impasse diplomático.
articles.body:
Os militares da Coreia do Sul afirmaram que a Coreia do Norte lançou mísseis balísticos em direção às águas a leste do país nesta segunda-feira (12), no horário local (noite de domingo, no horário de Brasília).

O lançamento dá continuidade a uma sequência recente de demonstrações de armamentos que elevou as tensões em meio a um longo impasse diplomático. Inicialmente, Seul havia informado a detecção de apenas um projétil, mas depois confirmou que se tratava de mísseis balísticos.

“Nossos militares detectaram, por volta das 9h20 (no horário local, 21h20 no horário de Brasília), vários mísseis balísticos lançados da região de Pyongyang em direção ao Mar do Leste”, afirmaram as Forças Armadas sul-coreanas em comunicado, referindo-se ao Mar do Japão.

“Nossos militares reforçaram a vigilância e o monitoramento diante da possibilidade de lançamentos adicionais”, acrescentou.

O Ministério da Defesa do Japão também informou ter detectado pelo menos dois lançamentos de possíveis mísseis balísticos e avaliou que os projéteis caíram em águas fora da zona econômica exclusiva do país.

O episódio ocorre dias depois de a Coreia do Sul testar em voo, na sexta-feira (10), sua primeira arma hipersônica, projetada para voar a uma velocidade de pelo menos cinco vezes a do som e escapar de sistemas de defesa antimísseis.

O presidente Lee Jae Myung descreveu o teste como um passo importante para fortalecer a capacidade de defesa convencional sul-coreana.

Ao mesmo tempo em que mantém uma postura linha-dura em relação a Seul, a Coreia do Norte vem intensificando os testes de armamentos enquanto busca ampliar seu arsenal de sistemas com capacidade nuclear.

Entre eles está um teste realizado em 3 de outubro do que Pyongyang descreveu como um míssil hipersônico de alcance intermediário, projetado para escapar dos sistemas de defesa antimísseis da Coreia do Sul e do Japão.

A Coreia do Norte também realizou outros testes de mísseis e exercícios com munição real, além de incorporar um novo navio de guerra, enquanto o líder Kim Jong-un continua exibindo seu programa de armas nucleares e rejeitando propostas dos Estados Unidos e da Coreia do Sul para retomar as negociações diplomáticas, paralisadas há muito tempo.

As tensões aumentaram ainda mais depois que três soldados sul-coreanos ficaram feridos na explosão de minas terrestres no mês passado, perto da fortemente militarizada fronteira entre as duas Coreias.

Os militares da Coreia do Sul e o Comando das Nações Unidas, liderado pelos Estados Unidos, concluíram que as explosões foram causadas por artefatos instalados pela Coreia do Norte, que negou responsabilidade e rejeitou os pedidos de desculpas.

articles.title: Comerciantes projetam aumento de 5% nas vendas no Dia das Crianças | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa do Sincomércio aponta que 78% dos consumidores pretendem gastar até R$ 250. Brinquedos lideram a intenção de compra.
articles.summary: Os itens mais procurados, de acordo com o Sincomércio, são os brinquedos, seguidos pela categoria de roupas, calçados e acessórios.
articles.body:
O comércio da Baixada Santista espera crescimento de 5% nas vendas para o Dia das Crianças, celebrado em 12 de outubro, na comparação com o mesmo período de 2025. Ao mesmo tempo, 78% dos consumidores da região pretendem gastar até R$ 250 com os presentes.

Os dados fazem parte de uma pesquisa do Sindicato do Comércio Varejista da Baixada Santista e Vale do Ribeira (Sincomércio), realizada com empresários e consumidores da região.

Os brinquedos lideram a intenção de compra para o Dia das Crianças, citados por 72% dos consumidores. Em seguida aparecem roupas, calçados e acessórios infantis, com 69%. As duas foram as únicas categorias presentes em mais de 50% das respostas.

Bicicletas, patinetes, bolas e itens esportivos: 39%

Eletrônicos leves e acessórios tecnológicos: 35%

Experiências e ingressos para atividades de lazer: 32%

Comerciantes da Baixada Santista projetam aumento nas vendas. — Foto: Alexsander Ferraz/ATribuna

A pesquisa também apontou a expectativa de gastos com os presentes. A maioria dos consumidores, 78%, pretende desembolsar até R$ 250, enquanto 22% esperam ultrapassar esse valor.

articles.title: Simaria volta aos palcos após quatro anos e fala sobre Simone | G1
articles.standfirst: Cantora gravou novo DVD com 13 músicas inéditas. Ao Fantástico, ela falou sobre a pausa na carreira, a dedicação aos filhos e o apoio da irmã.
articles.summary: Cantora gravou novo DVD com 13 músicas inéditas. Ao Fantástico, ela falou sobre a pausa na carreira, a dedicação aos filhos e o apoio da irmã.
articles.body:
Simaria voltou aos palcos após quatro anos. A cantora gravou um novo DVD, com 13 músicas inéditas, e anunciou a turnê Tô Bem. Em entrevista ao Fantástico neste domingo (11), ela contou por que decidiu se afastar da carreira. “Eu precisava cuidar de mim, da minha saúde mental, do meu corpo, olhar para mim um pouco e olhar para os meus filhos”, disse.

A artista também falou sobre o fim da dupla com Simone, anunciado em 2022. Ela revelou que enfrentava um período difícil emocionalmente. Apesar da separação profissional, as irmãs continuam próximas.

“Hoje, nós temos uma relação melhor do que quando a gente cantava juntas”, afirmou.

Segundo Simaria, as duas trocam conselhos e opiniões sobre as músicas que estão produzindo.

Simaria se emocionou ao lembrar dos anos dedicados aos filhos. “Eu pararia mil vezes, mil vezes, se fosse para ficar perto deles, porque eu pude viver os melhores momentos da minha vida”, declarou. A cantora também destacou o apoio da família. “Eles me salvaram, assim, primeiro Deus e depois minha família.”

Antes de subir ao palco, Simaria recebeu uma ligação de Simone. A irmã desejou boa sorte e comemorou o retorno. “Você vai arrasar. Nós todos esperamos por esse momento e você sabe o quanto eu torci por isso”, disse.

A gravação reuniu fãs de diferentes regiões do Brasil. A nova turnê está prevista para 2027.

articles.title: Pesquisa inédita encontrou munições compradas pelo Exército em apreensões ligadas ao Comando Vermelho | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do Instituto Sou da Paz analisou mais de 31 mil cartuchos de fuzil em 29 casos pelo país. Quatro em cada dez munições apreendidas com a facção eram de fabricação nacional.
articles.summary: Levantamento do Instituto Sou da Paz analisou mais de 31 mil cartuchos de fuzil em 29 casos pelo país. Quatro em cada dez munições apreendidas com a facção eram de fabricação nacional.
articles.body:
Uma pesquisa inédita do Instituto Sou da Paz identificou munições de fuzil compradas pelo Exército Brasileiro em apreensões ligadas ao Comando Vermelho. O levantamento analisou registros de mais de 31 mil cartuchos intactos, apreendidos em diferentes estados brasileiros.

Segundo o estudo, quatro em cada dez munições apreendidas com integrantes da facção nos casos analisados eram de fabricação nacional. Os pesquisadores também identificaram que parte dos cartuchos havia sido produzida pouco tempo antes das apreensões.

O levantamento foi feito a partir do cruzamento de laudos periciais e processos judiciais. A análise revelou padrões que se repetem em diferentes estados e dificuldades para identificar como munições adquiridas legalmente chegaram às mãos de criminosos.

Há cerca de 20 anos, a munição nacional comprada por forças de segurança passou a ter um código de rastreabilidade gravada em cada cartucho. Com isso, as munições encontradas em uma cena de crime conseguem ser identificadas. Porém, não há registro de possíveis repasses ou compradores destes armamentos.

O estudo descobriu que parte das munições usadas por criminosos para atacar policiais durante a megaoperação realizada no Rio de Janeiro, em 2025, pertencia às próprias forças de segurança.

Os pesquisadores também analisaram uma carga de 1.804 cartuchos interceptada no Distrito Federal, em 2019, que tinha como destino o Rio de Janeiro. Entre as munições, havia lotes do Exército, das polícias militares do Distrito Federal e do Rio de Janeiro, do Fundo Estadual de Segurança de Mato Grosso e do Ministério da Justiça, que já haviam aparecido em outras apreensões.

"Isso diz pra gente que essa fonte de desvio é uma fonte grande, é uma fonte que envolve bastante gente, mas que não conseguiu ser totalmente desbaratada pela polícia", explica Bruno Langeani, consulto do Instituto Sou da Paz.

Pesquisa mostra que munições compradas pelo exército chegam ao crime organizado — Foto: Reprodução/Fantástico

Em janeiro de 2025, uma investigação policial em Fortaleza, no Ceará, revelou um plano do Comando Vermelho para resgatar presos de uma unidade prisional do estado. Durante o monitoramento de integrantes da facção, policiais penais da inteligência foram surpreendidos por homens armados. Um agente morreu e outro ficou ferido. Quatro presos vão a júri popular pelo caso.

Na ação, a polícia apreendeu 400 cartuchos de fuzil. Segundo o Instituto Sou da Paz, fotografias da apreensão mostravam caixas com embalagens originais de munição brasileira, mas essas informações não foram incluídas no inquérito policial, o que impediu uma tentativa de rastreamento.

O pesquisador Bruno, do Instituto Sou da Paz, explicou que, mesmo quando há investigação sobre a origem das munições, nem sempre é possível identificar o caminho percorrido pelos cartuchos. Em muitos casos, as instituições conseguem confirmar a compra e o recebimento do material, mas não sabem informar como ele foi distribuído depois de chegar aos depósitos.

A organização diz que está cobrando o exército para que a lista dos códigos dos compradores seja disponibilizada publicamente. "A sociedade tem direito de saber o que está sendo feito com uma munição que foi comprada com recurso público", diz o consultor.

A Polícia Militar do Distrito Federal disse que “os protocolos internos de controle, armazenamento e carga de munições foram revisados e aprimorados, com o objetivo de fortalecer os mecanismos de fiscalização".

Já o o Exército disse que “reconhece a gravidade dos fatos relacionados ao extravio ou furto de munições e reforça que não compactua com desvios de conduta. A fim de coibir irregularidades e garantir que o rastreamento seja cada vez mais preciso, há uma constante revisão dos procedimentos de controle. Caso haja indícios de irregularidades, o Exército determina a abertura imediata de procedimento investigatório, como o Inquérito Policial Militar (IPM), com a finalidade de elucidar os fatos, recuperar o material e responsabilizar os envolvidos, atuando em estreita colaboração com os órgãos de segurança pública".

Também por nota o Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública disse que “o desvio de armas e munições legais para a ilegalidade é um dos focos da política de controle responsável de armas e munições, retomada pelo Governo Federal em 2023. O Ministério seguirá aprimorando com os demais órgãos, os mecanismos para identificar a origem das armas e munições que chegam ao crime organizado.”

articles.title: Manipur on edge after fresh killings; 9 killed in 12 hours, shutdowns disrupt key highways
articles.summary: Manipur hill districts remain tense after 9 killed in ethnic clashes across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul; shutdowns disrupt NH-2 and NH-202, security stepped up.
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Manipur’s hill districts remained tense on Sunday after nine people were killed in 12 hours of ethnic violence across Kamjong, Kangpokpi and Ukhrul districts on Saturday.Additional security forces were deployed in the affected areas of Kangpokpi and Kamjong districts, while separate shutdowns disrupted traffic on National Highways 2 and 202.The Committee on Tribal Unity (CoTU) called a 24-hour strike from Saturday evening. The Kuki CSOs Working Committee, Ukhrul, also enforced a shutdown in Ukhrul over the killings and its allegations of involvement by Naga militants and security personnel. No fresh fatality was reported on Sunday.CM Yumnam Khemchand Singh condemned the killings of civilians and appealed for restraint and dialogue. “CM has instructed the authorities concerned to take immediate and effective steps to tackle the situation, restore peace and order, and ensure the safety and security of all citizens,” the CM’s office said.The Kuki Chiefs’ Association, Manipur (KCA-M), on Sunday condemned what it called a “pre-planned attack” on unarmed civilian protesters in Chassad Kuki village in Kamjong district on Oct 9 and 10. It alleged that cadres of the NSCN (I-M), NSCN (Eastern Flank) and ZUF-K, in collusion with Tangkhul IRB personnel posted in the district, carried out the attack.“In this cowardly attack, the armed groups opened fire on civilian protesters and burnt down houses in Chassad village, resulting in the killing of Domkhonei Touthang and Michael Ngamminlen Haokip, both innocent Kuki civilians of Chassad village, and the destruction of houses,” the KCA-M said in a statement.The association claimed that the latest incidents took the number of Kuki civilian victims killed in attacks allegedly led by Tangkhul-led NSCN groups since March 11 this year to 30.The KCA-M demanded the immediate registration of FIRs for murder, arson and criminal conspiracy against the alleged perpetrators and the “involved IRB personnel”, along with their arrest. It also sought ex gratia payments of Rs 30 lakh each and govt jobs for the next of kin of the deceased, besides full compensation and the urgent reconstruction of the burnt houses.“Centre and security forces must understand the ground reality and secure all Kuki villages in Kamjong, Ukhrul, Tamenglong and Noney districts with adequate deployment of central forces to prevent further attacks,” the KCA-M said. It reiterated its demand for a separate union territory with a legislature for the Kuki-Zo people under the Constitution, saying this was necessary for lasting peace and security.The 12-hour outbreak of violence claimed six Naga lives, two Kuki lives — including that of a mother of five — and the life of a Gorkha farmer. Gunfights and arson targeting homes and shops were reported across the three districts, marking one of Manipur’s deadliest outbreaks of violence in the past year.Meanwhile, the working committee of the Tangkhul Naga Long (TNL), the apex traditional body of the Tangkhul Naga community, condemned the attacks on Tangkhul Naga civilians and alleged repeated aggression against border villages in Kamjong.“The external aggression against the border Naga villagers of Kamjong by the Kuki war parties has become a routine affair since the outbreak of violent conflict in the hills of Manipur,” it said.“In spite of the grim and alarming situation along the India-Myanmar border, the current political dispensation at Imphal and New Delhi has become a helpless spectator to the cross-border terrorism, while wilfully leaving their innocent citizens at the mercy of the foreign aggressors,” the organisation alleged.The TNL urged the authorities to take measures to protect residents living along Kamjong district’s porous international border.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Guwahati | Silver Rate in Guwahati | Bank Holidays in Guwahati | Public Holidays in Guwahati | Guwahati AQI | Weather in Guwahati | Petrol Price in Guwahati | Diesel Price in Guwahati | CNG Price in Guwahati | LPG Price in GuwahatiStay updated with the latest Guwahati news. articles.title: Muezzin arrested, cop suspended for ‘loud’ azaan in UP
articles.summary: Bijnor: DM, SP hear loud azaan; muezzin jailed, mosque loudspeaker seized, constable suspended; police order affidavits on noise limit compliance.
articles.body: BIJNOR: A mosque muezzin was arrested and sent to jail after Bijnor DM and SP heard an allegedly loud azaan while travelling to a public grievance hearing in Najibabad on Saturday. Police seized the mosque’s loudspeaker and suspended a beat constable for negligence.The incident also prompted a district-wide order requiring police stations to submit affidavits confirming that loudspeakers at religious places complied with prescribed noise limits.DM Umesh Pratap Singh and SP Krishna Kumar Bishnoi were passing through Mohalla Maqbara on their way to a Samadhan Diwas hearing when they heard the azaan being played at an allegedly excessive volume.Bishnoi directed Kotwali police to take action, following which station in-charge Amit Kumar Malik reached the mosque, seized the loudspeaker and detained muezzin Mohammad Faizan.On a complaint by sub-inspector Saurabh Kumar, police registered an FIR against Faizan for allegedly violating noise pollution norms.They also initiated proceedings against him for breach of peace, following which a sub-divisional magistrate’s court sent him to jail. Police subsequently suspended beat constable Lalit Kumar for allegedly failing to enforce noise restrictions in the area.Following the incident, police directed all station in-charges across Bijnor to submit affidavits through their beat constables certifying that loudspeakers at religious places in their jurisdictions operated within permissible limits.They warned that future violations could invite action against the station in-charge and beat personnel concerned.The action followed a district-wide police drive against loudspeakers at religious places in Sept, during which authorities reportedly removed 2,509 loudspeakers, including 1,323 from mosques, 1,116 from temples and 70 from gurdwaras.Religious institutions were also instructed to ensure that remaining loudspeakers operated within prescribed noise limits.Additional SP Krishna Gopal Singh said police were conducting a district-wide campaign to enforce govt and court directions on noise pollution.“Loudspeakers operating beyond the prescribed noise limits will not be allowed at religious places. Caretakers of all religious institutions have been instructed to follow the rules. Police station in-charges have also been directed to ensure compliance in their respective areas,” he said.In an Oct 1 order concerning a mosque in Saharanpur, Allahabad high court directed authorities not to interfere with the five daily azaans as long as the mosque complied with noise pollution rules.The court reiterated that using loudspeakers was not an essential religious practice protected under Article 25 of the Constitution and that their operation remained subject to the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Meerut | Silver Rate in Meerut | Bank Holidays in Meerut | Public Holidays in Meerut | Meerut AQI | Weather in Meerut | Petrol Price in Meerut | Diesel Price in Meerut | CNG Price in Meerut | LPG Price in MeerutStay updated with the latest Meerut news. articles.title: ​CJP's Abhijeet Dipke misses grandma’s funeral; Delhi Police and family trade charges
articles.summary: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke missed his grandmother’s funeral after Delhi Police detention; family and police dispute if he was informed and aided in time.
articles.body: CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke’s family cremated his paternal grandmother, nearly 24 hours after her death, in Hingoli district on Sunday, before he could return home following his detention, and release, by Delhi Police.The death has triggered a bitter clash of narratives between Dipke’s family and Delhi Police over whether authorities informed him in time and facilitated his journey home.On Sunday morning, Abhijeet Dipke’s mother, Anita, accused Delhi Police of preventing the family from contacting her son and denied police claims that he had been adequately informed about his grandmother’s death.Delhi Police rejected the allegation. “The information regarding the demise of Dipke’s grandmother was promptly conveyed to him with due sensitivity. He was also informed of the scheduled funeral time and offered all possible assistance to facilitate his travel to his hometown on humanitarian grounds. However, he denied to avail the same,” Delhi Police said in a social media post.Police also released CCTV footage from the detention facility to support their version.Dipke, who reached Nagpur on Sunday afternoon while travelling to his native village in Hingoli district after his release, contested the police account. He alleged that officers refused to let him speak to his cousin, who lived with his grandmother, and denied him access to his phone.“I was asking for my phone so I could retrieve my cousin’s number. Delhi Police has deleted that portion of the CCTV footage,” he alleged. In a social media post, Dipke accused the police of showing little compassion during his detention.“The same Delhi Police which is now taking the moral high ground for informing me about my grandmother’s demise and offering me a ride home came to me at 3.30am with arrest papers and demanded that I sign them. Where did all that humanity go at 3.30am? Even after knowing I had lost my grandmother, they insisted that I sign the papers. I refused until I was allowed to speak to my lawyers,” he wrote.The dispute added a fresh political edge to an already tense standoff between Dipke and authorities. Emerging from detention, Dipke said the CJP would resume its protests and declared that he had not signed any undertaking promising to stay away from future agitations. “Put me in jail a hundred times. We are not afraid of your dictatorship. We will end this dictatorship,” he told reporters in Nagpur.Earlier, he had posted on social media that the party would neither “back down nor be intimidated”, describing Oct 10 as “the beginning of the end of this dictatorship.”Stay updated with the latest Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar news. articles.title: Don't detain peaceful protesters, says SC; hundreds still taken away on Day 2
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Sunday sought responses of Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi metro rail chief D
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Sunday sought responses of Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi metro rail chief D Thara to a contempt petition for prima facie violating the court's Oct 9 order against complete shutdown of metro and train services in Delhi on Saturday to thwart CJP's protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The court also said lawyers, journalists, and other professionals should not be hindered in performing their duties "in any manner whatsoever".On the ground, nearly 700 people were detained (police claimed 400), many far away from protest zones, while barricading and traffic curbs remained on the roads much like Saturday. Protesters changed strategy, staging flash protests in small numbers at short notice. Most of the action was in and around CP as small groups of protesters kept trickling in. They were detained.Around 2.30pm, All India Student Association members, including president Neha Bora, started a protest near RK Ashram Marg metro station. As detentions began, Bora and a few others broke away and ran towards CP, where they continued to protest before being detained. Around 7pm, Students Federation of India members gathered at CP to hold a women's tiranga march against alleged police excesses, especially against women protesters. They were detained and taken away in buses. "How can they detain women at 7pm in the evening?" SFI general secretary Srijan Bhattacharya said.The widespread detentions - 7,000 estimated Saturday - figured prominently in arguments by the lawyers at SC's unusual holiday hearing on Sunday. Following the submissions, a bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "...we are of the opinion that the petitioners have made out a prima facie case. Accordingly, we issue notice upon the alleged contemnors". It asked them to file their responses by Oct 13.Normalise internet connectivity, ensure free movement in city: SCWe understand the gargantuan magnitude of detentions. We will have to seek a response from govt," the bench said after hearing the petitioners, who included advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, CPM MP M A Baby, RJD MP Manoj Jha and lawyer intervenors like Shadan Farasat, who was detained along with other advocates outside SC on Saturday.The bench asked for normalisation of internet connectivity and prohibition of "illegal" detentions, especially of those who gather for peaceful protest away from areas where prohibitory orders are in force. "There shall be no illegal detentions, particularly in cases of peaceful unarmed assemblage of people beyond the area where prohibitory orders under Sec 163 of BNS are in force," it said.On Oct 9, SC had restrained authorities from resorting to blanket closure of metro stations, though it said operations could be regulated depending on the situation. The order came after DMRC said 57 stations would be shut; that number was later revised to 45.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta disputed allegations of violation of the Oct 9 order and said Delhi Metro was functioning normally, though 45 out of 303 stations were closed to maintain law and order. He refuted the allegation that metro stations were closed, saying that "all metro stations are open since 10pm Saturday, trains are operating normally and internet connection has been restored".SC also issued directions to ensure free movement in the city subject to law and order situation/traffic regulations and that installing barricades shall be reviewed forthwith to ensure free movement subject to law and order and traffic requirements. "Lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in discharge of their professional duties in any manner whatsoever," SC said, and also directed withdrawal of prohibitory orders around SC and courts to facilitate free access to litigants and lawyers.Over 100 lawyers led by senior advocate and MP Kapil Sibal slammed the police brutalities on protesters, and accused authorities of continuing with the shutdown of metro and train services in complete disregard of the SC order and of illegal detention of protesters even in areas where the prohibitory orders were not in force.Sibal argued that internet shutdown was a blow to fundamental right to free speech and flagged detention of lawyers who participated in the protest. Senior advocate Farasat, who was detained, informed SC he was manhandled and bundled into a police vehicle. Senior advocate and TMC MP Menaka Guruswamy termed the entire episode as "undeclared emergency" worse than what Indira Gandhi had imposed (in 1975).When Sibal thanked the bench for holding court on Sunday because of the extraordinary turn of events, Justice Bagchi said, "We are always at the service of the nation." Later, Justice Bagchi said, "We know things have deeply affected you (the lawyers) and we do not want to trivialise anything."The bench issued notice to Centre and Delhi Police on a habeas corpus petition questioning detention of TMC politicians Mamata Banerjee, Derek O'Brien and Dola Sen. Solicitor general Mehta said the petition has become infructuous as the detained leaders were released last evening.As the pro-protest petitioners backed by a team of senior advocates - K K Venugopal, N Hariharan, Shoeb Alam, Arundhati Katju, G Sankaranarayanan, Sanjay Hegde - made a concerted attempt to corner police and Centre by flagging police action, senior advocate Kirti Uppal struck a discordant note by arguing that lawyers should not be stepping into shoes of their political affiliation."I was told that a lawyer's job is inside the courts and not on the streets," he said. The pro-protester lawyers inside the courtroom shouted 'shame, shame' to silence him. The bench asked the lawyers to maintain decorum of the courtroom and maintain silence.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Hyderabad man among 13 killed in Houthi strike on Saudi airport
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: An Indian national was among 13 people killed in one of the deadliest attacks launched by Iran-backed Houthi militants on Riyadh's King Khalid
articles.body: NEW DELHI: An Indian national was among 13 people killed in one of the deadliest attacks launched by Iran-backed Houthi militants on Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport Saturday. The Indian embassy also confirmed that 11 Indians were among the more than 300 who were injured.The Indian who died is a 46-year-old man from Hyderabad. According to sources, Mohammed Yusuf, an IT professional from Mehdipatnam, was waiting with his family near a check-in kiosk to travel to Madina for Umrah when a projectile struck the airport premises. Debris from the impact reportedly fell on Yusuf, leaving him critically injured. He later succumbed to his injuries at a hospital. His wife and two children, who were with him at the airport, are reportedly in critical condition.Ministry of external affairs (MEA) strongly condemned the repeated attacks on Riyadh's main airport over the past few days, including the "dastardly attack" on Oct 10. The ministry said in a statement that repeated attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure are completely unacceptable and must cease immediately."We stand in solidarity with the people and the govt of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia in defence of their sovereignty, and hope that peace and normalcy returns to the region at the earliest," said the ministry, while expressing condolences to the families of the deceased and wishing a speedy recovery to the injured in the attack.This was the second time India had condemned attacks on Saudi airports in the past few days, expressing solidarity with Riyadh. The dead from the third attack this week on the airport included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. articles.title: Por que Nossa Senhora Aparecida é negra? Veja o que explica a cor | G1
articles.standfirst: Escultura encontrada no Rio Paraíba do Sul, em 1717, passou por transformações ao longo de mais de três séculos; contato com a água e fumaça de velas estão entre as hipóteses para a tonalidade escura.
articles.summary: A imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida negra passou por transformações após ser encontrada no Rio Paraíba do Sul, envolvendo o contato com a água e a fumaça de velas.
articles.body:
Imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida — Foto: Thiago Leon/Santuário Nacional

A imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, santa Padroeira do Brasil celebrada nesta segunda-feira (12), é conhecida pela pele escura e pela importância religiosa que tem para milhões de fiéis. Mas você já se perguntou por que a santa tem essa aparência?

Encontrada por pescadores no Rio Paraíba do Sul, em 1717, a imagem passou por mais de três séculos de transformações. Historiadores e pesquisadores apontam que a tonalidade escura pode estar relacionada tanto às condições às quais a escultura foi submetida ao longo do tempo quanto à exposição à fumaça de velas.

A resposta, no entanto, não é tão simples. A história da imagem reúne registros históricos, hipóteses sobre sua conservação e diferentes interpretações sobre o significado que ela adquiriu para os brasileiros.

A imagem de Nossa Senhora da Conceição Aparecida é feita de terracota, um tipo de argila cozida. A autoria não é confirmada, mas a escultura é frequentemente atribuída ao Frei Agostinho de Jesus, religioso associado à produção de imagens sacras no período colonial.

Estudos sobre a peça indicam que ela originalmente tinha pintura, mas não há consenso absoluto sobre sua aparência inicial. Registros históricos antigos também não descrevem de maneira uniforme a cor da imagem, que aparece em documentos com referências a tonalidades como morena e parda escura.

A historiadora Tereza Pasin, que explica a história da imagem em reportagens do g1, aponta a possibilidade de a escultura ter sido produzida por Frei Agostinho de Jesus, com argila proveniente da região de Santana de Parnaíba, no interior de São Paulo.

Imagem da santa foi encontrada no rio Paraíba do Sul em 1717 — Foto: Divulgação/Arquidiocese de Aparecida

Água do rio e fumaça de velas: por que ela escureceu?

Duas explicações são frequentemente mencionadas para a tonalidade escura da imagem. Uma delas considera as condições às quais a escultura foi submetida antes e depois de ser encontrada. O contato prolongado com a água e a lama do Rio Paraíba do Sul pode ter contribuído para a perda da pintura original e para as alterações na superfície da peça.

Outra hipótese está relacionada à exposição à fumaça das velas acesas pelos devotos. Durante décadas, a imagem permaneceu em um ambiente de oração iluminado por velas e candeeiros, cuja fuligem pode ter contribuído para intensificar sua coloração escura.

As duas explicações aparecem em relatos sobre a história da imagem, mas não devem ser tratadas como uma conclusão definitiva sobre todas as mudanças pelas quais a escultura passou.

A pesquisadora Rachel Abdala, que também abordou o tema em reportagem anterior do g1 , ajuda a contextualizar como a imagem atravessou diferentes períodos históricos e adquiriu novos significados religiosos e culturais.

Imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida — Foto: Getty Images via BBC

A história do encontro no Rio Paraíba do Sul

Segundo a tradição católica, a imagem foi encontrada em outubro de 1717 por três pescadores que tentavam conseguir peixes no Rio Paraíba do Sul, na região de Guaratinguetá, no interior de São Paulo.

Depois de várias tentativas sem sucesso, um dos pescadores retirou das águas o corpo de uma pequena imagem. Em seguida, encontrou a cabeça. Após reunir as duas partes, os homens teriam conseguido pescar uma grande quantidade de peixes.

O episódio passou a ser associado a um milagre e marcou o início da devoção a Nossa Senhora Aparecida. A notícia se espalhou pela região, e a imagem passou a reunir cada vez mais fiéis.

Ao longo dos anos, a devoção cresceu até que Nossa Senhora Aparecida se tornou Padroeira do Brasil. O dia 12 de outubro, data dedicada à santa, é celebrado em todo o país e atrai milhares de peregrinos ao Santuário Nacional, em Aparecida.

Romeira reza com imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida — Foto: Carlos Santos/G1

A imagem também carrega uma história de identidade

Além das explicações sobre a transformação física da escultura, a cor de Nossa Senhora Aparecida ganhou um significado que ultrapassa a própria história material da peça.

Para muitos devotos, a imagem negra representa identificação, acolhimento e pertencimento. Sua importância também é discutida em reflexões sobre a presença negra na história brasileira, marcada pela escravidão e por desigualdades que persistem até hoje.

A forma como a imagem é percebida mudou ao longo dos séculos. Pesquisas sobre sua trajetória mostram que ela não permaneceu isolada das transformações sociais, culturais e religiosas do país. Assim, a pergunta sobre por que Nossa Senhora Aparecida é negra envolve tanto a história de uma escultura de mais de 300 anos quanto os sentidos que milhões de brasileiros atribuem a ela.

Há 46 anos, imagem de Nossa Senhora Aparecida, Padroeira do Brasil, foi quebrada em mais de 200 pedaços durante atentado na Basílica; relembre — Foto: Foto 1: Thiago Leon/ Santuário Nacional de Aparecida | Foto 2: Arquivo Pessoal/ Maria Helena Chartuni

A imagem foi restaurada após ser quebrada

Em 1978, a imagem sofreu um ataque e foi quebrada em numerosos fragmentos. A peça passou por um trabalho de restauração para que pudesse ser reconstruída.

O episódio marcou a história da escultura e exigiu um cuidadoso trabalho técnico para reunir os pedaços e recuperar sua estrutura. Desde então, a conservação da imagem é fundamental para preservar um dos símbolos religiosos mais conhecidos do Brasil.

Mais de três séculos depois de ser encontrada no Rio Paraíba do Sul, Nossa Senhora Aparecida continua no centro da devoção católica brasileira.

articles.title: The Asian silktree was brought to America for its delicate pink flowers; its seeds can remain viable for up to nearly 150 years under dry storage
articles.summary: Few garden trees look as graceful as the silktree in midsummer, when its fern-like leaves carry soft pink pompom flowers that seem to float above the
articles.body: Few garden trees look as graceful as the silktree in midsummer, when its fern-like leaves carry soft pink pompom flowers that seem to float above the branches. That beauty explains why people carried the tree across the ocean from Asia centuries ago and planted it beside homes and in gardens. Yet the same traits that made it appealing, including fast growth, abundant seeds, and tolerance of poor conditions, also allowed it to wander beyond yards. Today it appears along roadsides, in old fields, and at forest edges.How this pink-flowering Asian silktree arrived in North AmericaThe US Department of Agriculture states this tree does not belong to North America. It is native to Asia and occurs from Iran to Japan, and its scientific name is Albizia julibrissin. The review lists mimosa and silky acacia as other common names, and it notes that the genus is sometimes spelt with a double z, likely because the genus honors a man who introduced silktree to Tuscany, Italy. Silktree is a deciduous, nitrogen-fixing tree or shrub, usually between three and fifteen metres tall, with a broad crown. Its showy flowerheads form clusters at the ends of branches, and each head holds fifteen to twenty-five flowers.Why the 1745 introduction date is often repeated while another source places the arrival around 1785The US Department of Agriculture treats the arrival date with care. It states that silktree was introduced as an ornamental in the eighteenth century, and it acknowledges that many sources assert a specific year, 1745, for its introduction to the United States. It then adds a different account from Cothran, who wrote that the tree was brought to North America about 1785 and was first offered for sale in 1807. Either account places the introduction in the 1700s. By the 1950s, silktree was established locally in Georgia; it was a new record in Oconee County, South Carolina, in 1972, and it was first reported in the flora of Connecticut in 2008. In between, it was described as newly documented around Washington, District of Columbia, in 1995.How silktree took hold across the United States, from the Southeast to New York, Utah, and CaliforniaBy 2010, the US Department of Agriculture also reports silktree occurred as far north as New York and Massachusetts, in southern parts of the Midwest, throughout the south-central and southeastern United States excluding tropical Florida, and in New Mexico, Arizona, Utah, and California. The distribution and effects of silktree are best documented in the Southeast, where inventory data collected from 2001 to 2008 showed it is most common in north-central Alabama. Cold limits the tree to low elevations. In the Southeast, it does not typically grow above about 900 to 1,000 metres, and in Great Smoky Mountains National Park it was common between 370 and 610 metres and absent above 740 metres. Cold also matters in Connecticut, where it typically kills seedlings in their first winter, although silktree has established near the milder coast.Why silktree thrives on disturbed roadsides, old fields, and forest edges via seeds and root sproutsSilktree reproduces from seeds and regenerates by sprouting from roots after the top of the tree is killed or injured. Several authors note that it produces many seeds, and one source reports 8,000 seeds a year. Seeds fall mainly by gravity and secondarily travel by wind, water, and animals, with observations in Georgia suggesting wind can carry them at least ninety metres. A hard seed coat keeps seeds dormant until damaged by heat, fungi, soaking, or acid, and a small percentage of seeds kept in dry storage stayed viable for seventy to nearly one hundred fifty years. The circumstantial evidence suggests disturbance aids seedling establishment, and it describes silktree as an early to mid-successional species found on old fields, old homesites, roadsides, and woodland edges.Why silktree populations rise and fall: short lifespans, a root-infecting fungus, and shade toleranceSilktree is not an unstoppable force, and the US Department of Agriculture explains why. It is apparently short-lived in the United States because a soil-borne fungus called Fusarium infects the root system, causing wilting and eventually death. Researchers around Athens, Georgia, suggest silktree often dies back within ten to twenty years, while another report gives an average lifespan of about thirty years. Even so, trees killed by the wilt disease may leave behind a mass of root sprouts. Silktree also tolerates only partial shade and rarely occurs under a full canopy, which is why it favours open and disturbed ground. It may establish or increase on recently burned, thinned, or logged forest sites, and it was considered a potentially high threat to oak-hickory woodlands.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A 48-year-old man died following an alleged assault inside a Delhi Metro train over a seat reserved for senior citizens, prompting Delhi Metro
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A 48-year-old man died following an alleged assault inside a Delhi Metro train over a seat reserved for senior citizens, prompting Delhi Metro Police to arrest a 65-year-old retired IAS officer and his 36-year-old son.The accused, Sanjay Pratap Singh and Sidharth Singh, both residents of Noida, have been remanded to 14-day judicial custody.A police officer said the incident took place on Oct 8 when the victim, Pawan Sharma, was travelling with his mother Durga Devi, 65, towards Yamuna Vihar. According to police, an argument broke out over the senior citizen seats after Singh and his son boarded the train at Mandi House. Sharma and his mother were seated on seats designated for senior citizens. “A dispute arose between Sharma and the father-son duo over the seat. The argument escalated into a physical altercation,” police said.When the train reached Supreme Court metro station, Sharma reportedly became unconscious. Information about an unconscious passenger on platform 1 was received at Supreme Court Metro police station around 5.47pm. By the time police reached LNJP Hospital, where Sharma had been taken with his mother, doctors had declared him brought dead,” a senior police officer said.Sharma had gone to Gurgaon with his mother to visit his brother and was returning home when the incident occurred. Sharma’s mother Durga claimed that when the metro reached the Supreme Court station, two men approached them. “They rudely asked us to vacate our seats. We got up, and my son then told them they could now lie down on the seats. The older man grabbed Pawan (Sharma) by the collar and slapped him. When he objected, the man’s son assaulted him. When I tried to intervene, the older man restrained my arm.”During the preliminary inquiry, police recorded the statement of Sharma’s mother. A case was registered based on her statement under Sections 105 and 3(5) of BNS, relating to culpable homicide not amounting to murder and acts committed with common intention.Investigators examined the circumstances surrounding the altercation and the alleged involvement of the two accused. At 2.51 pm, Bora posted: "We have crossed the barricades and reached CP."Police personnel pursued the demonstrators through the streets before intercepting and detaining them. Cops were seen holding them by their arms and legs while dragging and carrying them towards waiting buses even as they kept struggling and resisting.In a video posted on X after her detention, Bora alleged that agitators were being held in cramped compartments inside a police bus. "These are the buses they are taking us in. This bus has four cells," she said. "There is no space to breathe."She claimed the windows had glass behind metal grilles and that several women were confined together in a small compartment. She also alleged that male protesters had been verbally abused and kicked in their private parts. Questioning the conditions in which they were being transported, she likened the compartments to jail cells and accused police of using excessive force.The attempted march followed a series of appeals by Bora to sustain the protests despite police curbs. Earlier Sunday, she had written on social media: "When those sworn to protect the Constitution look away, people must remind them what it demands. We cannot let this become normal. The fight for democracy continues, and we will not look away."Her call for Sunday's gathering followed a late-night post urging supporters to continue demonstrating despite Saturday's detentions."Let a hundred Jantar Mantars bloom! articles.body: One person was killed and 11 others injured in a fresh attack on Riyadh's international airport on Sunday, Saudi authorities said, a day after a strike claimed by Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi rebels killed 13 people and injured more than 300.Saudi-led coalition forces in Yemen said an unidentified projectile struck Terminal 4 of King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, triggering a fire.Saudi air defences also intercepted a cruise missile near the airport, destroyed a drone in the Eastern Province and intercepted a ballistic missile fired towards Khamis Mushait.Meanwhile, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority confirmed a strike on Dammam airport late Sunday, saying damage assessments and safety inspections were under way.An eyewitness aboard an aircraft taxiing at Dammam airport told Reuters that a projectile struck the tarmac near several parked aircraft at around 8.30pm local time, triggering a fire. The aircraft returned to the gate, and passengers were asked to disembark and leave the area.The death toll from attacks on Saudi airports rose to 18 over the week. Saturday's strike on Riyadh airport killed 13 people, including four Saudi nationals, while the remaining victims were foreign nationals, Saudi authorities said. Indian national Mohammed Yousuf, 46, was among those killed.Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed responsibility for Saturday's attack in a televised address on Sunday. He also said the group had targeted King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, in the Eastern Province, and two facilities belonging to Saudi oil giant Saudi Aramco.Earlier on Sunday, the Houthis renewed their warning against the use of Saudi airports, saying Riyadh would be responsible for any failed interceptions.Britain's embassy in Saudi Arabia advised its citizens to avoid all but essential travel to Jeddah, Dammam and all airports in the kingdom except Medina airport.US aviation authorities also issued a notice urging American airlines to exercise caution when flying to or over Saudi Arabia.You use AI every day. articles.title: WordPress cofounder Matt Mullenweg is buying Stewart Brand’s 1912 Sausalito houseboat; Mirene was once a gasoline schooner and later became a restored home on the water
articles.summary: Matt Mullenweg, the cofounder of WordPress and chief executive of Automattic, is set to acquire Mirene, a historic houseboat that has been home to Whole
articles.body: Matt Mullenweg, the cofounder of WordPress and chief executive of Automattic, is set to acquire Mirene, a historic houseboat that has been home to Whole Earth Catalog creator Stewart Brand and his partner, Ryan Phelan, for decades. Built in Coos Bay, Oregon, and completed in 1912, Mirene was originally a gasoline schooner intended to serve canneries in Alaska. It was converted into a diesel tugboat in the 1930s. Mullenweg confirmed in a September 11 blog post that he had made an offer for the vessel, and The San Francisco Standard reported on September 16 that the deal was under contract. The purchase also involves the couple’s smaller houseboat, although the agreed price for the vessels has not been disclosed. For Brand and Phelan, the planned sale marks the end of a long chapter shaped by restoration, life on the water and their connection to Sausalito’s distinctive houseboat community.A century-old tugboat with an unusual historyMirene is no ordinary houseboat. Brand and Phelan acquired the vessel in the early 1980s and spent decades restoring it, adapting it into a home while retaining its ability to sail. Its history and seaworthiness distinguish it from the stationary houseboats around it. According to The San Francisco Standard, Mirene is the only houseboat in Sausalito permitted to leave its dock. The couple spent years restoring and adapting the vessel for life on the water. Its working-boat origins remain part of its character, setting it apart from the stationary houseboats around it.The vessel also carries a piece of music lore. According to The San Francisco Standard, a wooden table added by the couple is supposedly where Otis Redding sat while writing “(Sittin’ on) the Dock of the Bay” during a stay on a nearby houseboat. The anecdote adds to Mirene’s appeal, although the precise connection between the table and the song remains a reported story rather than an independently established fact. The smaller houseboat included in the planned transaction offers a different arrangement. Unlike Mirene, the smaller houseboat is stationary. The San Francisco Standard described it as having a well-lit living area. Mullenweg has said he hopes to blog from Mirene’s kitchen table, making the vessel both a place to live and a setting for his writing. In an earlier interview with The San Francisco Standard in November 2025, Phelan discussed the sense of loss associated with parting with the vessel.From $1.8 million to a $1 million asking priceThe planned sale followed an extended period on the market. Mirene was initially listed for $1.8 million before its asking price was reduced by $100,000 in July. In August, the price fell again to $1 million. The smaller houseboat’s asking price also fell from $700,000 to $450,000, according to its listing. The reductions did not establish the final sale price. When The San Francisco Standard reported the deal on September 16, the transaction was under contract, and the parties had not disclosed the amount agreed upon.Compass real estate agent Steve Sekhon told the publication that the boats had attracted no offers for almost a year, despite their refurbished condition. He said the price reduction helped bring the listings greater visibility. The report also described improving activity in the local houseboat market, with sales generally closing slightly below asking prices. The smaller vessel was described by real estate agent Steve Sekhon as a potential privacy buffer for the buyer of Mirene or a separate waterfront retreat for someone seeking a home in the Sausalito area. For a buyer interested in the area’s houseboat lifestyle, the two properties offer different ways to experience it: one aboard a vessel with a history of sailing, the other in a stationary home on the water.A houseboat purchase amid upheaval at AutomatticThe purchase comes as Mullenweg navigates a period of corporate turmoil. In September, Automattic’s board voted to place him on paid leave as CEO, temporarily naming chief financial officer Mark Davies as interim chief executive. Mullenweg returned to the role roughly 33 hours later, after the attempted leadership change unravelled. The attempted leadership change was followed by the departure of directors involved in the dispute, with those departures reported around September 14. Automattic announced a new board on September 25, according to TechCrunch. Automattic is the parent company of WordPress.com, Tumblr and WooCommerce, among other businesses.Despite the disruption, Mullenweg has publicly embraced the prospect of taking on Mirene. In his September 11 blog post, Mullenweg wrote about the prospect of owning the vessel and the lessons he expected to learn from maintaining it. He also wrote that he hoped to do a lot of blogging from the kitchen table. Brand and Phelan now live primarily on a waterfront property in Petaluma, while Phelan has also bought another Sausalito houseboat, allowing her to maintain a connection with the community. Mullenweg has expressed the hope that he can eventually pass Mirene on to another steward decades from now.For now, the proposed sale brings together two people with an interest in independent publishing and the unconventional spaces in which creative work happens. If completed, the transaction will give Mullenweg a historic vessel shaped by more than a century of use, as well as a new place to write and live on the water. Brand, meanwhile, has said he expects the boat to bring its new owner good luck.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.summary: KOCHI: Three youths were killed when a speeding Mini Cooper, driven by Alappuzha South native Sajeev Jamal's son Suhail (19) rammed their scooter at
articles.body: KOCHI: Three youths were killed when a speeding Mini Cooper, driven by Alappuzha South native Sajeev Jamal's son Suhail (19) rammed their scooter at 1.45am on Sunday on the airport road along Nedumbassery.Police arrested an 'inebriated' Suhail on charges of culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The deceased were identified as Devika (21) of Wayanad, Gopika (22) of Palakkad and Iyas (21) of Coorg, Karnataka.CCTV footage showed the premium hatchback hitting the two-wheeler from behind and the passengers being thrown off on impact. The victims were killed on the spot and the scooter landed some distance away. People rushed them to Desom CA hospital and Angamaly Taluk Hospital where the youths were declared dead.Nedumbassery Police said that the trio were employees of a craft shop in Thrikkakara and had gone to a tea shop near the airport. They were heading to Athani when the car rammed their scooter. The front portion of the car was mangled in the crash.District Police Chief (Ernakulam Rural) KS Sudarshan said police took Suhail into custody from the spot and the team completed his medical examination immediately. He said they took blood and urine samples for forensic examination. Sudarshan said although the reports of his blood sample are awaited, preliminary probe indicated that he was inebriated. When asked if he was driving under the influence of other intoxicants, he said the police took samples to check the same and further action would be taken based on medical reports.Soon after the accident, videos from an Instagram page, purportedly belonging to Suhail, were shared widely on social media. One of them was an Instagram story that showed the car rocketing at a speed of 220km/hr during a highway ride. Sudarshan said his team had taken note of the incident and the driver's background will be investigated."We have cameras on these routes. If such activities happened in the past, we will investigate them," he said. Reacting to reports that Suhail's co-passenger had quarrelled with first responders, he said that they will collect statements and act accordingly. He added that further sections can be added against Suhail as and when an offence is detected. articles.title: Psychology says children who go grocery shopping with their parents may be learning a skill adults often overlook
articles.summary: A trip to the supermarket can easily turn into a negotiation over chocolates, biscuits and colourful packets.
articles.body: A trip to the supermarket can easily turn into a negotiation over chocolates, biscuits and colourful packets. Parents may be focused on finishing the shopping quickly, keeping the bill within budget and getting everything on the list. Children, meanwhile, may be asking why one packet costs more than another, whether they can pick the fruit, or why a favourite snack cannot go into the trolley.It may look like an ordinary family outing, but these small interactions can offer children opportunities to practise a skill they will need long after they stop accompanying their parents to the grocery store: making decisions.From choosing between two products to understanding that spending money on one thing leaves less for another, grocery shopping brings everyday choices into a setting children can see and participate in. With a little guidance, it can also become an opportunity to introduce early mathematical thinking, budgeting, planning and the ability to weigh options.The important part is not simply taking a child along. It is allowing them to participate in age-appropriate decisions instead of treating them only as passengers in an adult task.How grocery shopping can become a lesson in decision-makingChildren make choices throughout the day, but many decisions made at home are either taken on their behalf or presented as instructions. A grocery store offers a different experience: several options are visible, prices can be compared, and choices often have immediate consequences.Should the family buy apples or bananas this week? Is the larger packet necessarily better value? If the shopping list includes a few essentials, can an additional treat fit into the budget?These questions encourage children to look beyond what they want in the moment and consider what else matters.A 2025 study published in the journal Appetite, titled Examining the ability of children to make competent purchases in food retailing, investigated purchasing decisions among 692 children aged eight to 10. Researchers used a virtual supermarket simulation and examined factors including hunger, enjoyment, brand awareness, mathematical ability and financial planning.The findings suggested that mathematical skills and financial planning were associated with better purchasing decisions, including fewer impulsive purchases and more cost-effective choices. Hunger, on the other hand, was associated with poorer purchasing quality, while enjoyment was linked to better adherence to shopping lists.The study does not establish that accompanying parents to a supermarket directly improves decision-making. However, it highlights the kinds of abilities that matter when children have to make purchasing choices.For parents, the practical takeaway is to give children opportunities to think through a choice rather than simply telling them which product to pick. Asking, "Which of these two options do you think makes more sense, and why?" can be more useful than immediately supplying the answer.The aim is not to make a child responsible for family spending. It is to help them understand how choices are made.The hidden mathematics of a shopping trolleyA supermarket is full of opportunities to use mathematics without opening a textbook. Children can count the number of items in a basket, compare prices, estimate the total cost of a few products or check whether the change received at a shop is correct.Younger children can begin with simple comparisons: which packet contains more biscuits, which fruit costs less, or how many tomatoes are needed for the family. Older children can work with quantities, unit prices, discounts and a fixed spending limit.Research suggests that everyday conversations can help make these opportunities more meaningful.A 2019 study published in Mind, Brain, and Education, titled Promoting Math Talk in Adult–Child Interactions Through Grocery Store Signs, observed 179 adult-child pairs shopping in grocery stores. Researchers compared interactions in which signs encouraged mathematical conversations with interactions prompted by general-language signs or no signs.Adults exposed to the mathematics prompts talked about maths more often than those in the other conditions. The study showed that a simple change in the environment could encourage adults to bring mathematical ideas into an ordinary activity.It did not directly demonstrate long-term improvements in children's maths achievement. Nevertheless, it illustrates how easily a routine shopping trip can include opportunities to discuss numbers, quantities and comparisons.Parents do not need to turn every aisle into a classroom. A question such as "This packet costs ₹40 and that one costs ₹60. What is the difference?" may be enough. For a younger child, comparing the number of oranges or identifying shapes and colours can be just as appropriate.The idea is to make numbers part of everyday conversation rather than something children encounter only during homework.Why choosing between products can teach children about moneyMoney can feel abstract to children when they hear adults discuss salaries, bills or monthly budgets. At a store, however, they can see the relationship between a price tag, a purchase and the amount of money available.For example, parents can explain that the family has planned to buy certain essentials first and can spend a limited amount on additional items. An older child might compare two similar products and calculate which offers better value. A younger one might be asked to choose one fruit from two options.These small decisions can introduce the idea that money involves trade-offs. Choosing one item may mean postponing another, and the cheapest option is not always the most suitable one.A 2025 study available through Developmental Psychology research literature examined how parents of toddlers and preschoolers talked about money during pretend grocery shopping. The paper, Money talks! The role of parents' discussion of money for preschoolers' math knowledge, discusses how familiar activities involving money can provide opportunities to practise mathematical concepts in meaningful contexts.The research supports the importance of examining how parents talk about money with young children. It should not be interpreted as proof that a single grocery trip will make a child financially literate.For parents, this can mean explaining everyday financial decisions in simple, non-alarming language. Instead of saying, "We cannot afford anything you want," a parent could explain, "We have planned our spending for today, so let's choose one thing from this section."Children can learn that money is a resource to plan with, not simply something that appears when they ask for a product. There is no need to share adult financial worries or make children anxious about household expenses.What happens when children ask for something parents do not want to buy?One of the most familiar supermarket scenes involves a child asking for a snack and a parent saying no. It can be tempting to see the exchange as a distraction from the real task of shopping. Yet the way parents handle these disagreements can also offer children a chance to understand boundaries, preferences and negotiation.A 2006 study published in the Journal of Nutrition Education and Behavior observed 142 adult-child shoppers across 11 supermarkets in the Minneapolis–St Paul metropolitan region. In 67 of 133 observations, children initiated a request. Of those requests, 55.2% were for sweets or snacks, and adults agreed to nearly half of the requests.The researchers also noted that explaining a refusal was among the strategies parents used when declining a child's request. They suggested that grocery shopping could offer opportunities for adults to reinforce children's interest in food and nutrition.The findings describe shopping interactions rather than proving which parenting response produces the best long-term outcome. Still, they point to a useful distinction: saying no does not have to end the conversation.A parent might explain that the family already has snacks at home, that the item is not on the list, or that the child can choose a snack for another day. The explanation can be brief and consistent.Children may still protest, and parents do not need to change their decision to prevent disappointment. Learning to accept a limit is part of dealing with choices in the real world.At the same time, parents can avoid turning every request into a battle. Offering two acceptable options can allow a child some control without handing over the final decision.Let children participate, but do not expect them to behave like adultsChildren's ability to understand prices, compare products and anticipate consequences develops over time. A preschooler may understand that they can choose one fruit but may not grasp the difference between a discount and a genuine saving. A school-age child may be able to calculate a total but still be influenced by attractive packaging or hunger.A study published in Young Consumers examined seven families over 19 grocery-shopping trips and found that children influenced their parents both directly and indirectly. Their requests and negotiation strategies varied, as did their parents' responses.The study's small, qualitative sample means its findings cannot be generalised to every family. It nevertheless illustrates that shopping is an interaction in which children observe adults, express preferences and learn how decisions are negotiated.Parents can adapt the experience to a child's age and temperament:For toddlers and preschoolers: Ask them to identify familiar foods, count a few items or choose between two suitable options.For children aged five to eight: Give them a short shopping list, ask them to locate products or compare quantities and prices with help.For older children: Let them plan a simple meal, estimate its cost, compare unit prices or manage a small, clearly defined budget.Safety and practicality matter, too. A crowded store, a rushed trip or an overtired child may not be the right setting for a learning exercise. Parents can keep the task short and step in when needed.The goal is not a perfect shopping tripTaking children grocery shopping will not automatically make them better decision-makers. The benefits depend on what they are allowed to do, what adults explain and whether children get opportunities to think rather than simply follow instructions.A parent who completes the entire trip while a child sits in the trolley may offer little opportunity for participation. Another parent who invites the child to find three items, compare two products or explain a choice creates small moments for practice.And children will not always make the choice an adult would make. They may choose the brightly coloured packet, miscalculate a price or change their minds. These are not necessarily signs that the exercise has failed. With age-appropriate guidance, they can become moments to explain, reconsider and try again.The larger lesson is that children do not learn every important life skill through formal lessons. Some begin with ordinary family routines: planning a meal, sorting laundry, helping in the kitchen or accompanying a parent to the market.The next time a child asks to put something in the trolley, parents can pause before either agreeing or refusing. A simple question - "Why would you choose this one?" - may reveal how the child is thinking and give them a chance to explain it.The grocery list may still be the adult's responsibility. But learning to weigh options, understand limits and make a reasoned choice is a skill children can gradually begin practising beside them.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: ‘Unofficial house arrest’: After release, YouTuber Dhruv Rathee claims cops still stationed outside Gurgaon home
articles.summary: GURGAON: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was prevented by police from joining Saturday's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest, described his detention as an act
articles.body: GURGAON: YouTuber Dhruv Rathee, who was prevented by police from joining Saturday's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest, described his detention as an act of 'kidnapping'.Rathee, an Indian citizen who lives in Germany and came here for the protest, said in a video post he was released by cops around 3am on Sunday after being held in detention for over 20 hours without access to a lawyer or phone.He also alleged his parents were manhandled during the detention, accusing the Centre of creating an "unofficial Emergency".In the video, posted at 11.19am on Sunday, Rathee alleged that he was forcibly taken from his bedroom without even being allowed time to wear his slippers. He also claimed that he was assaulted and had sustained injuries all over his body."These people have literally sent 'gundas' to kidnap me. There were more than 50 'gundas' outside my house... I was dragged from my bedroom like a criminal," he said.According to sources, Rathee returned to his parents' house in Kendriya Vihar, Sector 56, on Sunday morning amid police presence, with around 50 personnel in plain clothes gathered near his apartment complex.The detention came amid protests in Delhi led by the CJP demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The demonstrations on Saturday were met with extensive security arrangements, barricading, traffic restrictions and detentions of protesters.Recounting the events of Saturday morning, Rathee alleged that around 20 men in plain clothes entered his house around 7am while he was still asleep. His mother, who opened the door after hearing a commotion outside, was allegedly pushed aside as the group entered the house and moved towards his bedroom."Before I could react, these people literally kidnapped me. The operation did not follow procedure expected during an arrest or detention. They literally dragged me out of the bedroom, took me down the stairs. I have injuries all over my body," he alleged.Rathee claimed that even his parents' phones were seized, leaving them unable to record the incident. The YouTuber was kept in detention at Sector 39 crime branch after he was picked up from his home."They kept me confined for 20 hours, neither allowed me to access a phone, nor allowed me to speak to a lawyer. The police personnel kept telling me that it was neither an arrest nor a detention and that I would be released." Rathee said in the video.Questioning the circumstances in which he was taken from his home, Rathee said he would have accompanied the police willingly had an officer identified himself, explained the legal provisions, and asked him to visit a police station.He claimed that around 15 police personnel had been stationed around his house after his release, monitoring his movements and effectively placing him under what he described as unofficial house arrest.He said he would not back down. "I will continue to raise my voice for the country in this same way no matter how much you try to suppress me," he said.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news.
