articles.title: ASI gunned down in Tarn Taran; 5th cop to be murdered in Punjab this year
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) with the counter-intelligence wing was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne assailants while returning home
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: An assistant sub-inspector (ASI) with the counter-intelligence wing was shot dead by two motorcycle-borne assailants while returning home after duty late Sunday evening. Iqbal Singh (55) is the fifth policeman to be murdered in Punjab this year.A resident of Naushera Pannuan, around 15 km from Tarn Taran, Iqbal sustained at least two bullet injuries in the attack, and died on the spot. The killers sped away and are yet to be identified.Tarn Taran SSP Surendra Lamba said, "The ASI was posted in Makhu (70 km from Amritsar). He was being followed by two bike-borne assailants who shot two to three bullets at him between 6:15 pm and 6:30 pm on Louhka Road in Tarn Taran district. We have got some leads and hope to trace the accused soon."As per initial information, the ASI was driving back after a "private visit" and wasn't in uniform, said the SSP.A senior police officer said Iqbal’s nephew is Ajmeet Singh, an accused in the 2022 Sarhali police station RPG attack case, who was shot dead in Naushera Pannuan on Sept 11 while on bail.According to sources, investigators are examining if the two murders are connected. The accused in Ajmeet’s killing was injured in a police encounter and arrested. “We are investigating the organised crime angle and revenge killings by gangsters,” said a senior police officer.Police are also examining a social media post in which gangsters Doni Bal, Prabh Dasuwal, Mohabbat Randhawa, Afridi Toot, Amar Khabbe and Shaganpreet purportedly took responsibility for Iqbal’s murder.The post claimed that the ASI was close to “our rival Landa Harike”, and hinted at a revenge killing over the murder of a sarpanch. The same group had claimed responsibility for Ajmeet’s murder.The slain ASI was earlier posted in Ferozepur counterintelligence and had been transferred to Tarn Taran recently. “There is a high probability this was a targeted killing by an organised crime network. We are investigating the case from all angles,” said the SSP.The murder is the latest in a series of attacks on police officials in Punjab. On Feb 22, ASI Gurnam Singh and home guard Ashok Kumar were shot dead inside a police station in Gurdaspur.On May 24, ASI Joga Singh was shot dead in Majitha and on Sept 17, ASI Harjit Singh was shot dead in Amritsar. On Sept 12, ASI Jaswant Singh narrowly survived a murder bid in Amritsar, and on Oct 4, ASI Sukhchain Singh was injured after being shot at in Ajnala.The attacks have triggered criticism from opposition parties. Former Punjab Congress chief Amarinder Singh Raja Warring said, “Punjab is bleeding, and Bhagwant Mann’s govt has serious questions to answer... Repeated shootings and killings are creating fear across Punjab. Bhagwant Mann, how many more lives must be lost before your govt wakes up? When police personnel themselves are being targeted, what sense of security can ordinary citizens expect?”Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon posted on X: “In a Punjab where even those in uniform are not safe, who can the common Punjabi rely on? On one side, grand advertising claims about law and order; on the other, blood spilling on the streets. AAP has completely failed on the law and order front.”SAD functionary Bikram Singh Majithia alleged that CM Bhagwant Mann has “badly failed to maintain law and order in Punjab”. “CM is busy criticizing opponents and entertaining people with jokes while murderers continue to ambush and attack our police personnel… Arvind Kejriwal is taking Punjab back to the era it was engulfed in violence,” Majithia tweeted.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Experts say AI may change the price of food and groceries: What is good and bad for customers
articles.summary: Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations.
articles.body: Food retailers are rapidly adopting artificial intelligence (AI) to run their operations. While the technology promises inventory efficiency and targeted discounts, economists and legal scholars warn it could also usher in an era of personalised and dynamic pricing – fundamentally altering what shoppers pay for everyday essentials.How AI is entering the grocery aisles and popular food chainsAccording to CNBC, retailers worldwide are testing and expanding data-driven systems at multiple touchpoints. US grocer Kroger introduced FlashFood, an AI platform that spots perishable items nearing their expiration dates, reduces their prices, and notifies shoppers via an app. Major chains in the US, including Kroger, Walmart, Whole Foods and Amazon Fresh are also rolling out digital screens to replace paper price tags, as are UK grocers Tesco, Morrisons and Asda. These digital tags enable stores to update shelf prices remotely in seconds.Financial platform Revolut recently tested facial-recognition checkouts at select coffee shops, letting buyers pay with a glance. In the UK, Sainsbury’s launched “SmartLists,” an AI tool that converts photos or meal ideas into curated shopping lists.Recently, an antitrust lawsuit accused McDonald’s of using an AI-driven “pricing engine” to determine menu rates across US stores and allegedly overcharge customers for staples like Big Macs and french fries. McDonald’s denied using AI to calculate what individual customers are willing to spend, asserting that it merely offers franchisees "tools, resources, research and recommendations to help them make informed decisions."What experts say about dynamic pricingAs automated infrastructure expands, experts caution that retailers have the tools to adjust pricing in real time based on demand patterns.“Dynamic pricing means changing prices in response to changing market conditions, such as demand, timing, capacity or competitors’ prices. It is not new. Airlines, hotels, and ride-hailing services have used it for years,” Miroslava Marinova, senior lecturer of commercial law at the University of East London, was quoted as saying.However, the rapid collection of granular personal data, which includes purchase records, browsing history, device location and buying routines, is beginning to blur the lines between broad market shifts and personal profiles.“Dynamic pricing responds primarily to market conditions, whereas personalised pricing uses information about the consumer to estimate willingness to pay. As retailers combine market-level information with increasingly detailed consumer data, the boundary between dynamic and personalised pricing becomes thinner,” Marinova explained.What is good and bad for shoppersAlgorithmic pricing is not inherently harmful to household budgets, the report said. Algorithms can lower prices on overstocked or aging inventory, curbing food waste and offering cheaper options for budget-conscious buyers. As a result, when discounts are applied strategically, certain foods and grocery services become more accessible to lower-income segments.However, there are some risks involved. The downside of individual-level pricing models centers on transparency and market fairness. When prices fluctuate continuously, shoppers cannot tell whether a price tag reflects general market supply or their personal browsing profile.“If consumers cannot understand why they received a particular price, cannot compare it with prices offered to others, and cannot effectively switch to another supplier, the normal disciplining effect of consumer choice becomes weaker,” Marinova warned.The Bank of England economists pointed out that when prices change constantly and differently for every shopper, measuring inflation becomes difficult.You use AI every day. articles.title: Syria has reopened a 1,600-year-old church complex after an extensive restoration and war-clearance work bringing Byzantine history back to life
articles.summary: An outstanding piece of early Christian history has reopened to visitors in northern Syria.
articles.body: An outstanding piece of early Christian history has reopened to visitors in northern Syria. It will offer a fresh opportunity to explore an ancient religious complex that has survived natural calamities like earthquakes, wars and centuries of changes. The Deir Samaan Citadel, associated with Saint Simeon the Stylite and also known as Qalaat Semaan, welcomed visitors again on September 28, 2026 after massive restoration work.Situated in the countryside of Aleppo, the historic site is as old as the fifth century. Its monumental church, monastery, baptistery and processional route once formed an important destination for Christian pilgrims. Today, the complex is part of the Ancient Villages of Northern Syria, a collection of archaeological sites recognised on UNESCO’s World Heritage List in 2011.It’s a significant step in efforts to protect Syria’s cultural heritage.Why is this ancient church complex special?The story of the complex starts with Saint Simeon the Stylite, who was a Christian ascetic. He became famous for spending decades living on top of a pillar. As per historical records published by Syria’s Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums, Simeon was born around 386 AD.He gradually raised his pillar to a height of approximately 18 metres, attracting followers and visitors who came to hear him preach. After his death in 459 AD, the location became home to his religious teachings and ascetic life.Between 476 and 490 AD, during the reign of Byzantine Emperor Zeno, an enormous church complex was built around the pillar. The design featured four basilicas arranged around an octagonal central space. It was a monumental architectural wonder. The complex subsequently expanded to accommodate a baptistery, monastery and accommodation for visitors. It was a massive structure for its time.From a pilgrimage destination to a fortified citadelOver the years and centuries, the place experiences extreme natural disasters and war and changing regimes.Earthquakes between 526 and 528 AD damaged the site. As per official reports, the church's wooden dome above the octagonal section collapsed and was never replaced.Later in the 10th century, Byzantine forces fortified the hill and turned the complex into a stronghold. This military phase gave rise to the name Qalaat Semaan, or the Citadel of Simeon. The fortress subsequently changed hands during regional conflicts and gradually lost its military importance. But later it fell into disuse.What restoration work was carried out?According to Syria's state news agency, SANA, the restoration work included repairing visitor routes and facilities, rehabilitating the main square and reinforcing sections considered structurally vulnerable. Officials also reported work to return the Column of Saint Simeon to its location.An important heritage siteDespite its historical importance, the Saint Simeon complex has suffered considerable damage in recent decades all because of the conflict in Syria. It placed archaeological sites across the country at risk from military activity, looting and neglect. According to the site's official historical timeline, the surviving column associated with Saint Simeon was damaged in an airstrike in 2016.The February 2023 earthquake caused further destruction, bringing down the entrance arch and columns of the western section's narthex. These incidents added to the damage accumulated over many centuries.A report prepared by Syria's Directorate-General of Antiquities and Museums for UNESCO in 2026 described serious structural vulnerabilities at Qalaat Semaan, including damage to the church and baptistery. The reopening is therefore an important step towards the site's recovery.Can visitors explore the complex again?The September 2026 reopening has restored public access to the historic complex, allowing visitors, researchers and people interested in archaeology to reconnect with the site. Deir Samaan's reopening is also part of a broader effort to revive tourism in Aleppo province.For now, the return of visitors to the Saint Simeon complex represents a meaningful moment for one of the region's most distinctive historical landmarks.You use AI every day. articles.title: Britain once used this 2,000-acre coastal site for secret weapons testing; abandoned military buildings now stand among marshes, birds and deer
articles.summary: Orford Ness, a remote stretch of the Suffolk coast in eastern England, holds a combination of military history and protected wildlife.
articles.body: Orford Ness, a remote stretch of the Suffolk coast in eastern England, holds a combination of military history and protected wildlife. Covering more than 2,000 acres, the shingle spit was once a closely guarded testing ground where British researchers worked on aircraft, radar and nuclear weapons technology. Today, its landscape contains abandoned concrete laboratories, former airfield marshes and fragile coastal habitats supporting birds, hares and deer. According to the National Trust, which now manages the nature reserve, the site offers a rare opportunity to explore how decades of secret military activity shaped this landscape.How did Orford Ness become a secret weapons testing siteOrford Ness was not always a military installation. As the National Trust explains, salt marshes developed behind the growing shingle spit during medieval times, eventually providing grazing land for local communities. Walls were built around parts of the marshes to control tidal water, while sheep and cattle continued to graze there for centuries.The area's strategic importance also grew from its coastal position. Suffolk's beaches and deep estuaries made the region potentially vulnerable to invasion, and the nearby coastline was involved in military preparations during earlier conflicts.The decisive change came in 1913, when the War Department purchased a large part of Orford Ness before acquiring the entire site soon afterwards. The National Trust records that the land became a military testing ground, with access restricted to protect the work taking place there.Between 1913 and 1916, sections of King's Marsh were drained and levelled to create airfields. The first aircraft arrived in 1915, marking the beginning of decades of military experimentation. History Hits’ account of Orford Ness also describes how the isolated location made it suitable for closely guarded projects during both world wars and the Cold War.What experiments took place behind the fencesThe testing programme expanded well beyond aircraft operations. According to the National Trust's history, the site became an important centre for experiments involving aircraft performance, weapons and military detection systems.One notable structure is the Bomb Ballistics building, completed in 1933. Researchers used specialist equipment there to record the flight of bombs, helping them understand how bombs travelled through the air and improve the calculations used for aiming. The work continued for more than four decades, with later developments contributing to research associated with atomic weapons.Orford Ness also played a significant role in the development of radar. In 1935, Robert Watson-Watt and his team arrived to establish what was presented as an ionospheric research station. The National Trust explains that this was a cover for work on an aerial defence system that became known as radar.Other experiments examined how vulnerable aircraft and their components were to attacks. Between 1938 and 1959, controlled firing trials tested the effects of projectiles on aircraft, fuel tanks, oxygen tanks and engines. During the 1950s, the marshes were also used to study the flight paths of air-launched rockets.These activities left behind buildings and infrastructure that still reveal the site's former purpose, even though much of the work was conducted under strict secrecy.The concrete labs preserve a remarkable military legacyAmong the most striking remains are the buildings commonly known as the Pagodas. These concrete structures were built for atomic weapons research and testing, giving the landscape an appearance quite unlike that of a conventional nature reserve.The National Trust's history of Orford Ness describes the establishment of 6 specialised test cells by the Atomic Weapons Research Establishment, which was based at Aldermaston. Laboratory 1, completed in 1956, was used for mechanical and vibration testing, as well as drop tests. These facilities allowed researchers to examine how components behaved under different conditions.The National Trust explains that the former Control Room, also built in 1956, initially served Laboratory 1 before being adapted for the Hard Target Impact facility. Although the Control Room is no longer open to the public, it remains a reminder of the protective measures built into the research site.Another structure is the Black Beacon, completed in 1928. Its apparent purpose was to house a marine navigation beacon, but the National Trust explains that it actually accommodated equipment intended to help military aircraft find their way. The Bomb Ballistics building and the former Radar Receiver building provide further evidence of the wide range of experiments conducted on the Ness.History Hit reports that the atomic weapons establishment ceased work at the site in 1971. However, the landscape did not simply lose its historical significance when the experiments ended.Why has wildlife returned to the former military landscapeOrford Ness is now recognised for its ecological importance as well as its history. The National Trust describes it as an internationally significant coastal nature reserve, with more than 10 miles of coastline and over 2,000 acres of land.The area is particularly notable for its vegetated shingle, a rare habitat formed when the sea deposits stones into ridges and valleys over long periods. According to the National Trust, around 20% of Europe's vegetated shingle is found at Orford Ness. This fragile environment takes centuries to develop, and even a misplaced footstep can damage its delicate structures.Beyond the shingle, coastal grazing marshes and wetlands provide habitats for a variety of wildlife. The National Trust identifies wetland and wading birds, Chinese water deer and hares among the animals found across the reserve. Former airfield land has also become grazing marsh.Orford Museum describes the Ness as a remote wildlife haven and highlights its connection with Havergate Island and the wider Alde-Ore estuary.The contrast is particularly striking because the military buildings remain visible within the landscape.The reserve now combines conservation with historical discoveryThe National Trust took ownership of Orford Ness after its military use ended, bringing a new purpose to a place that had remained inaccessible to the public for decades. Its work now includes managing habitats, protecting the fragile shingle landscape and helping visitors understand the site's history.Visitors can explore designated walking routes through the former airfield, marshes and coastal habitats. The National Trust's structures guide describes the Red Route, which follows former airfield areas before crossing towards the vegetated shingle. Other routes open seasonally to protect breeding birds.The former Radar Receiver and NAAFI building now houses the Island of Secrets exhibition. According to the National Trust, it explores the site's military research from the First World War through to the Cold War, including accounts from people who worked there. A decommissioned atomic bomb is also part of the display.Access remains carefully managed. articles.summary: Japanese Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa called for stronger cooperation between oil-producing and consuming countries as well as greater oil stockpiling and i...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Japanese Trade Minister Ryosei Akazawa called for stronger cooperation between oil-producing and consuming countries as well as greater oil stockpiling and infrastructure development in Asia, seeking to strengthen the region's resilience to supply disruptions.

Energy security has become increasingly important amid heightened tensions in the Middle East, Akazawa said during an online appearance at the International Energy Forum ministerial meeting.

The push reflects Japan's efforts to reduce Asia's vulnerability to oil supply disruptions, particularly those stemming from instability in the Middle East. Under its POWERR Asia initiative, introduced in April, Japan is seeking to expand regional oil reserves, strengthen supply chains and improve emergency response capabilities through cooperation with energy-producing countries.

The minister also highlighted plans by the Asia Zero Emission Community, to deepen cooperation with oil-producing countries and strengthen coordination in emergencies.

Akazawa also said Japan aims to serve as a bridge between Middle Eastern oil producers and Asian countries, strengthening efforts between the regions and contributing to stable global energy supplies.

The IEF ministerial meeting brings together energy ministers from more than 60 major oil- and gas-producing and consuming countries for dialogue between producers and consumers. Governments, international organizations and companies discussed energy security, investment in sustainable energy and trade.

articles.title: A Texas home built in 1861 ranked third among America's haunted destinations; visitors report seeing a woman in white
articles.summary: A historic Texas home built in 1861 has secured the third spot on a national list of America's haunted destinations, drawing attention to its
articles.body: A historic Texas home built in 1861 has secured the third spot on a national list of America's haunted destinations, drawing attention to its centuries-old architecture and stories of unexplained encounters. Known as The Grove, the property stands in Jefferson, Texas. According to a report by MySA, the house featured in USA Today's 10Best roundup of haunted destinations. Visitors and people associated with the property have claimed to see a woman dressed in white, a mysterious figure walking through the garden and other unusual occurrences. While these accounts have contributed to The Grove's reputation, the reported paranormal experiences have not been scientifically verified.Inside the 1861 Texas home ranked among America's most haunted destinationsThe Grove, also known as the Stilley–Young House, is located at 405 East Moseley Street in Jefferson, Texas. It was built in 1861 by Frank and Minerva Stilley and is recognised for its historic architecture and reported paranormal activity.USA Today's 10Best roundup ranked The Grove third among America's haunted destinations, according to MySA. The first two places went to Zak Bagans' The Haunted Museum in Las Vegas, Nevada, and the Indiana State Sanatorium in Rockville, Indiana.Unlike purpose-built haunted attractions, The Grove is a historic residence that offers guided tours exploring its architecture, history and stories of reported supernatural encounters. Its combination of historical significance and local folklore has helped attract visitors interested in both history and the paranormal.The woman in white and other reported apparitionsThe most famous ghost story associated with The Grove centres on a woman dressed in white, often referred to as the Lady in White. According to the property's official website, a female figure has reportedly been seen following a recurring route through the house. The website associates the apparition with Minerva Fox Stilley, the wife of Frank Stilley, who built the house in 1861.According to the property's account, the woman appears to pass through a wall. The website suggests that this detail may relate to the building's earlier layout, when a doorway and porch occupied the area before alterations were made. In 1870, a room was added to connect the previously detached kitchen to the main house. Although this architectural history provides context for the legend, it does not establish that the reported apparition exists.Two other figures feature in The Grove's paranormal folklore. One is a man reportedly seen striding through the garden's lily beds as though he is hurrying somewhere. The other is described as a mischievous presence in the den, with some accounts portraying it as flirtatious towards women. These stories extend the reported encounters beyond the Lady in White and contribute to the house's reputation among visitors interested in paranormal folklore.A Texas home's haunted reputation dates back to the 19th centuryAccording to The Grove's official website, one of the earliest stories associated with the house dates to 1882, when a man named T.C. Burke reportedly bought the property and moved his family into it. The account says the family left soon afterwards, with the explanation recorded as: “We can't live there...” The website does not establish why the family departed, and independent corroboration of the episode has not been established.More recent accounts describe unusual experiences reported by the property's owners after they moved into the house in March 2002. A passage reproduced on The Grove's official tour page from Texas Monthly recounts claims that bedsheets were pulled away at night, the deadbolt on a kitchen door locked by itself and a dining-room mirror became covered in condensation. The accounts do not establish what caused these incidents.The tour page also recounts an incident involving a visitor who reportedly held out a tape recorder and invited any presence in the house to speak. Although no response was reportedly heard at the time, an old man's voice allegedly saying, “I miss my family,” was heard during playback. The recording has not been independently authenticated, so the account remains an anecdote rather than verified evidence of a supernatural voice.Other stories reproduced on the property's website describe objects being moved and mirrors coming off walls. The accounts, alongside the stories of the Lady in White and the other reported figures, have helped sustain interest in The Grove over the years. However, these experiences remain attributed claims and local legends, not independently established evidence of paranormal activity.The historic house has undergone several changesAlthough The Grove dates to 1861, the building has undergone alterations over the years. According to its official website, a room was added in 1870 to connect the previously detached kitchen to the main house.Further changes followed in the 1930s, when an indoor bathroom was installed and the side porch was enclosed. The property's history identifies these changes as part of the building's evolution while retaining its 19th-century character.Its historic designation provides a documented basis for its significance beyond its reputation as a haunted destination.The Grove is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has been designated a Recorded Texas Historic Landmark. Records maintained by the US National Park Service identify the Stilley–Young House as a historic property in Jefferson and document Greek Revival architectural influences.The Grove remains open for guided toursDespite its reputation, The Grove is not an abandoned building. It remains a private residence that welcomes visitors for scheduled guided tours.The property's official website describes an approximately one-hour experience covering the home's history and stories associated with its reported apparitions. The published schedule lists usual tour times of 2 pm on Saturdays and 11 am on Sundays, although schedules may change. Advance reservations are required, and visitors should confirm the latest timings directly with the property before travelling.Located in Jefferson, Texas, the house offers visitors an opportunity to explore a historic 19th-century building while hearing the accounts that have made it a destination for paranormal enthusiasts.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.body: New footage has been released by news outlet Al Arabiya showing the moment a strike hit King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, as passengers, including Umrah pilgrims preparing to board their flights, waited inside the terminal.The footage captures the moments surrounding the impact, bringing into focus the danger faced by civilians caught in the attack.The missile strike on Saturday, October 10, killed 13 people and injured more than 300 others, according to Saudi authorities. An Indian national was among those killed, while 11 Indians were injured, the Indian embassy in Riyadh said. The embassy said it was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to monitor the condition of the injured and provide assistance.The Indian national who died was identified as Mohammed Yusuf, a 46-year-old IT professional from Hyderabad. According to sources, Yusuf, who was from Mehdipatnam, was waiting near a check-in kiosk with his family to travel to Medina for Umrah when the strike hit the airport. Debris from the impact reportedly fell on him, leaving him critically injured. He later died in hospital. His wife and two children, who were accompanying him, were also injured and were reported to be in critical condition.In a statement issued after his death, the Indian embassy said it would support the family and facilitate the early repatriation of his mortal remains. External affairs minister S Jaishankar also condoled the death, saying the embassy would extend all possible assistance to the bereaved family.The Saudi civil aviation authority identified the other victims as four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals and one person each from Palestine, the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria and Sudan.The attack was followed by another incident on Sunday, when an unidentified projectile struck a passenger terminal at Riyadh airport, according to the Saudi-led coalition fighting Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. The projectile hit the complex housing terminals 3 and 4, which are used for domestic flights. Authorities did not immediately provide further details about Sunday's incident. The airport remained closed, while schools in Riyadh shifted to online classes.The latest incidents came amid repeated attacks targeting Saudi airports and oil installations. Yemen's Houthi movement, also known as Ansar Allah, has claimed responsibility for attacks on Saudi targets in recent days, but had not claimed responsibility for Saturday's deadly airport strike at the time of the reports.On Sunday, Houthi military spokesperson Brigadier General Yahya Saree warned airlines and travellers against using Saudi airports and airspace, saying they were vulnerable to attacks. Airports in Mecca and Medina were exempted from the warning.India's ministry of external affairs strongly condemned the repeated attacks on Riyadh's main airport, including the October 10 strike, describing attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure as “completely unacceptable” and calling for them to stop immediately. New Delhi also expressed solidarity with Saudi Arabia and called for peace and normalcy to return to the region.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Scottish couple bought 700 acres in Oregon in 1910 and built a ranch that became a community hub; their historic home is now a museum at a 40-million-year fossil monument
articles.summary: In the remote John Day River Valley of central Oregon, where neighbours could live dozens of miles apart, Scottish immigrants James and Elizabeth Cant
articles.body: In the remote John Day River Valley of central Oregon, where neighbours could live dozens of miles apart, Scottish immigrants James and Elizabeth Cant built a ranch that became an important gathering place for the local community. In 1910, the couple purchased approximately 700 acres and gradually expanded their property to nearly 6,000 acres, raising sheep and cattle, cultivating crops and maintaining orchards. Their large family home also accommodated travellers, ranch workers and schoolchildren, while its rooms hosted community gatherings. After James died in 1972 and Elizabeth in 1973, the family sold the ranch to the National Park Service (NPS) in 1975. The property subsequently became part of John Day Fossil Beds National Monument, where the historic house preserves the story of ranching and rural life in the region. The monument is also known for fossil deposits that document more than 40 million years of ancient life.Scottish immigrants in Oregon: how James and Elizabeth Cant built a successful ranch in the John Day River ValleyElizabeth Grant was born on 10 November 1885 in Moray County, Scotland. She was the youngest child of Mary Grant, who supported her family by working as a crofter, or tenant farmer, in Muir of Lochs, near Elgin. Elizabeth attended school until her teenage years, when she began working alongside her mother. James Cant grew up in Forres, Scotland, in a family headed by a widowed mother. In 1900, he left Scotland for Portugal and Argentina, where he worked with sheep and established a business selling mules. He eventually settled in central Oregon, and Elizabeth travelled there in 1907 to join him. The couple married in October 1908, according to the National Park Service's biographical account of Elizabeth Cant.During the early years of their marriage, the Cants worked for another Scottish rancher, Alexander Murray, with Elizabeth working as a cook. After earning money and acquiring sheep through their work, James bought land known as the Officer Homestead with a business partner. In 1910, the family established its own ranch on approximately 700 acres. They raised sheep, chickens and bees, maintained a vegetable garden and cultivated crops including alfalfa and barley. The property expanded over time to nearly 6,000 acres, according to the NPS's history of Cant Ranch. The Cants' story also offers a glimpse into the lives of Scottish immigrants who settled in central Oregon and helped shape the region's ranching communities.Cant Ranch history in Oregon: a family home, school and gathering placeBy 1917, the Cants had four children and regularly welcomed travellers moving between the valley and The Dalles. They also provided accommodation for several sheepherders working on the property. To accommodate the growing household and its visitors, the family commissioned plans for a larger house, built with lumber milled near Mitchell. The two-and-a-half-storey building, completed in 1917, remains a prominent part of the historic ranch complex. The house was designed around the practical demands of ranch life. During summer, women and girls in the household slept on the upstairs porch, while men and boys slept on the first-floor porch. Ranch workers stayed in the house or in a nearby bunkhouse. The surrounding grounds included a vegetable garden, fruit orchards, a hog pen and a chicken coop, while fields near the John Day River produced wheat, alfalfa and other crops.The house also played an important educational role. School was held in its third-floor attic until the nearby Cant School was built in 1919, and the local teacher lived with the family. Elizabeth also helped accommodate workers involved in road construction and hired some to carry out irrigation projects on the ranch, according to the NPS's Elizabeth Cant profile. Beyond its agricultural and domestic functions, the house became a social centre for the area's Scottish community. The Cants hosted gatherings featuring music, dancing and traditional Scottish dress. Their midnight suppers sometimes brought together more than 20 guests and continued until morning. Such events were significant in a sparsely populated valley where neighbours could live many miles apart.Throughout the 1920s and 1930s, the ranch supported hundreds of sheep, thousands of acres of land and dozens of employees and boarders. The family also planted apple and peach orchards. When sheep ranching became less profitable in the 1940s, the Cants shifted towards cattle, continuing the business with help from their adult children and their spouses. The ranch's history reflects both the family's commercial success and the role its home played in sustaining a dispersed rural community.From Cant Ranch to John Day Fossil Beds National Monument: preserving ranching history alongside fossilsJames Cant died in 1972, followed by Elizabeth on 15 May 1973. The National Park Service's biography of Elizabeth Cant states that the family sold the ranch in 1975. However, the park's Scope of Collection Statement records the acquisition of portions of the James Cant Ranch in 1976. John Day Fossil Beds National Monument was established on 8 October 1975 under legislation authorised on 26 October 1974, and the park was officially dedicated on 23 August 1978. The two NPS accounts give different dates for the sale and acquisition, without fully explaining the relationship between them. The ranch house and associated buildings subsequently became part of the monument's historic landscape and served park visitor services and administrative functions. The property is now part of the monument's Sheep Rock Unit. The approximately 200-acre Cant Ranch Historic District includes the main house and historic ranch structures, along with features associated with the property's agricultural history, such as irrigated fields and orchards. The district was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1984.Today, the Cant Ranch Historic Home and Museum interprets the Cant family's experience and the history of ranching in the John Day River Valley. Unlike the monument's main fossil visitor centre, the historic home has limited public access. According to the National Park Service's published information, it is generally closed in fall, winter and spring because of staffing shortages, with limited opening days in summer. Visitors should check the park's current operating hours before planning a visit.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: SBI warns customers of rise in Jumped Deposit Scam, here's what it is and his to stay safe
articles.summary: State Bank of India (SBI) has alerted the customers about the increasing online fraud known as the ‘Jumped Deposit Scam’.
articles.body: State Bank of India (SBI) has alerted the customers about the increasing online fraud known as the ‘Jumped Deposit Scam’. SBI has asked the customers to not trust unexpected credits received in their bank accounts and to remain cautious of suspicious payment requests. As part of the National Cyber Security Special Campaign 6.0, the country’s largest bank said that the fraudsters are using small deposits to gain the trust of victims before attempting to steal larger amounts via UPI payment requests. “Beware of Jumped Deposit Scam! In a Jumped Deposit Scam, scammers claim to have "accidentally" credited a small amount to your account to win your trust. When you try to return it, they trick you into approving a high-value payment request,” wrote SBI in a post shared on social media platform X (formerly known as Twitter).What is the Jumped Deposit Scam and how it worksAccording to SBI, the scam begins when fraudsters claim to have “accidentally” transferred a small amount of money into a customer's bank account. The scammer then contacts the victim and requests that the money be returned.However, instead of asking for a simple transfer, the fraudster sends a payment collect request or another transaction request designed to trick the victim into authorising a much larger amount than the original deposit. “Unexpected credit in your account? It's a trap!” SBI said in a post shared on social media, cautioning customers against acting on such requests without verification.The bank said scammers often use emotional manipulation, urgency, or emergency situations to pressure victims into approving transactions quickly. By first depositing a small amount, fraudsters attempt to make their story appear genuine and lower the victim's guard. Once the victim approves a payment request, the money is transferred out of their account, resulting in financial loss.SBI's advice to usersThe bank listed three precautions:* Block and report: Block the number immediately and report the incident to the bank on priority.* Resist pressure: Don't give in to emotional blackmail or emergency UPI requests without confirming them first.* Check the caller: Always respond to calls that begin with the prefix 1600. SBI says these are genuine and secure calls from the bank.Apart from this, it is also advisable to never approve any payment request that you didn't start yourself. Also, if you see a credit you can't explain, don't send anything back yourself. Contact your bank through its official number or branch and let it handle the reversal.You use AI every day. articles.title: In 2021, a Brisbane man bought his home; after nine structural defects led to a $500,000 repair estimate, a tribunal revived his warranty claim, though coverage may be capped at $300,000
articles.summary: A Brisbane homeowner has won a significant legal battle after a construction regulator rejected his claim for a property plagued by serious structural
articles.body: A Brisbane homeowner has won a significant legal battle after a construction regulator rejected his claim for a property plagued by serious structural defects, reopening the possibility of compensation for repairs estimated at more than $500,000. However, the outcome may still leave him facing a substantial financial burden. According to The Courier-Mail and realestate (dot) com, which reported the Queensland Civil and Administrative Tribunal’s decision, Anton Ady’s claim against the Queensland Building and Construction Commission (QBCC) was rejected over a procedural issue. The tribunal overturned that decision and sent the matter back to the regulator for reassessment. The QBCC’s published guidance confirms that its home warranty scheme generally provides up to $200,000 in standard cover, rising to $300,000 where eligible homeowners have purchased optional additional protection.Ady bought the Brisbane property on April 15, 2021. The house had been built by Classy Homes Pty Ltd during the pandemic, but subsequent engineering investigations identified multiple problems affecting the site’s stability and the building’s foundations. The builder later entered liquidation and its licence was cancelled, leaving Ady to seek assistance through Queensland’s statutory home warranty scheme.Nine defects raised serious structural concernsAn independent engineering assessment identified nine major defects, according to the tribunal findings reported by The Courier-Mail. These included deep voids beneath footpath slabs, where supporting materials had washed away and left gaps reaching approximately 550 millimetres.The assessment also identified failing retaining walls and boundary fences, movement in the deck, inadequately braced steel piers beneath the house and unstable soil around the main foundation supports. The combination of these problems raised concerns about further structural damage and the possibility of land movement. Repair estimates reportedly exceeded $500,000, covering the work needed to stabilise the site and reconstruct the foundations.With the original builder no longer operating, the homeowner turned to the QBCC for help under the Queensland Home Warranty Scheme, which provides a statutory safety net for eligible residential construction claims when licensed builders fail to complete work or rectify covered defects.Tribunal challenges regulator’s decisionThe dispute centred not only on the condition of the house but also on how Ady’s claim had been submitted. The QBCC had rejected the claim because he had not lodged its official online complaint form. However, Ady had previously provided engineering reports during legal proceedings in May 2023, setting out the defects affecting his property.The tribunal found that the information already supplied could satisfy the relevant statutory notification requirements. It rejected the argument that the absence of a particular form was sufficient grounds to dismiss the claim, emphasising that the regulator needed the information required to assess the matter. The tribunal also preferred the independent engineer’s evidence on structural issues over the assessment of a QBCC building inspector. Its decision means the regulator must reconsider the claim rather than rely on the original procedural rejection.The ruling does not, however, amount to an award covering the full repair bill. The QBCC has acknowledged the decision and said it is considering the matter, but a final resolution date has not been provided.Compensation may fall short of repair costsEven if Ady’s claim is accepted, statutory limits could prevent him from recovering the full amount required to repair the property. Standard cover for eligible defective-work claims is generally capped at $200,000. Homeowners who have purchased optional additional cover within the prescribed period may qualify for a higher limit of $300,000. Against an estimated repair bill exceeding $500,000, even the higher limit could leave a shortfall of more than $200,000, depending on the final approved claim and repair costs.Against an estimated repair bill exceeding $500,000, even the higher limit could leave a shortfall of more than $200,000, depending on the final approved claim and repair costs. The scheme is designed as a statutory safety net rather than comprehensive home insurance. Its limits mean that a successful claim does not necessarily guarantee full reimbursement for extensive structural damage. For Ady, the tribunal’s decision removes a procedural obstacle and gives his claim another chance. But until the QBCC completes its reassessment and determines the amount payable, the final cost of saving his home remains uncertain.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: In 2005, a Wonga Park home with a 160-metre miniature railway sold for A$420,000; 20 years later, the property with its electric train, tunnel and trestle bridge sold for A$1.375 million
articles.summary: A home in Wonga Park, a suburb of Melbourne in Australia, has a feature that sets it apart from an ordinary family property: a miniature railway running
articles.body: A home in Wonga Park, a suburb of Melbourne in Australia, has a feature that sets it apart from an ordinary family property: a miniature railway running through its garden, complete with an electric train, a tunnel and a timber trestle bridge. Located at 24 Dudley Road, the property sold for A$420,000 on January 20, 2005. Nearly 21 years later, it changed hands for A$1.375 million on December 6, 2025, according to Australia's primary digital property platform realestate.com.au. The difference between the two sale prices is A$955,000. The December 2025 price was more than three times the amount recorded in 2005. However, the property also underwent changes over the years, and the sale prices alone do not establish how much of the increase was attributable to the railway or other features.A 160-metre railway was part of the property in 2005As per the original listing on Australian residential property portal View, the listed house is an A-frame home on a block measuring nearly half an acre, with views towards Mount Dandenong. The advertisement highlighted five bedrooms, two bathrooms, a lounge and dining area with an open fireplace, and a separate family room adjoining the kitchen. The outdoor space was also a major selling point. The listing specifically advertised a 160-metre train track with a five-inch gauge, describing it as an attraction the whole family could enjoy. The property also had a patio, a garage and workshop, a carport, a wine cellar and additional storage. The railway was therefore not a feature added to the property shortly before its latest recorded sale. It was already being promoted as part of the home when it was marketed in 2005.What the property offered when it sold for A$1.375 millionAccording to the listing on realestate.com.au, the home sold for A$1.375 million on December 6, 2025. It sits on a 1,654-square-metre block and was marketed as a four-bedroom, three-bathroom house with two parking spaces. The sale listing described the miniature railway as an electric train set among landscaped gardens, with a tunnel and a timber trestle bridge. The backyard also featured a large lawn, mature fruit trees, a chicken coop and views across the surrounding treetops towards the Dandenong Ranges. Inside, the home had two substantial living areas, high vaulted ceilings, an open fireplace and an enclosed outdoor entertaining deck. The kitchen featured stone benchtops, an island breakfast bar, a butler’s pantry, a Miele dishwasher and AEG cooking appliances. The upper floor included a main bedroom with mountain views, a dressing room and an ensuite. The property also had a study, an attic room that could be used as a fourth bedroom or retreat, a cellar and a powered, plumbed workshop.The property’s appeal lies in the combination of a family home, landscaped outdoor space and a miniature railway that was already part of its identity more than two decades ago. Its sale history offers a glimpse of how the same distinctive feature has remained part of the property’s story across different listings and owners.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Melinda French Gates and her daughters backed a $70 million fund; 22 organisations received money to tackle women's health and violence
articles.summary: Melinda French Gates and her daughters, Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates, joined other philanthropists in backing a $70 million initiative to
articles.body: Melinda French Gates and her daughters, Jennifer Gates Nassar and Phoebe Gates, joined other philanthropists in backing a $70 million initiative to improve women's health and address gender-based violence. Launched in September 2025, the Women's Health Co-Lab brought together donors through ICONIQ Impact and Co-Impact to support 22 organisations working on maternal healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and violence prevention. The initiative aims to mobilise $100 million and provide three years of support through unrestricted grants, allowing recipients to direct resources towards their priorities. Its approach focuses on strengthening organisations and healthcare systems while addressing barriers that prevent women and girls from accessing essential services and living free from violence.How Melinda French Gates and her daughters backed the $70 million fundThe Women's Health Co-Lab was launched on September 29, 2025, by ICONIQ Impact, the philanthropic platform associated with investment firm ICONIQ, in partnership with Co-Impact, a global collaborative philanthropy organisation. The initiative brings together philanthropists to support organisations addressing persistent inequalities in women's health and safety.French Gates and her daughters were among the founding supporters, alongside other philanthropists and families. The initiative's initial commitments exceeded $70 million, with a broader target of raising $100 million. The funding was designed to support 22 selected organisations over three years, giving them resources to expand their programmes and strengthen the systems serving women and girls.Three areas the fund aims to addressThe Women's Health Co-Lab focuses on maternal health, sexual and reproductive health and rights, and gender-based violence. Its grants support organisations providing services, advocating policy changes and addressing barriers that affect women's wellbeing.Maternal healthSix organisations were selected to improve maternal healthcare, strengthen service delivery and help women access appropriate care during pregnancy and childbirth.One recipient is Every Mother Counts, a nonprofit working to make pregnancy and childbirth safer. Its work addresses barriers that prevent women from receiving quality maternal healthcare, including gaps in access, resources and support.Sexual and reproductive health and rightsTen organisations will work to expand access to reproductive healthcare, contraception, reliable information and related services. Their work also includes advocacy to address policies and social barriers that restrict women's ability to make decisions about their health.Among the named recipients are Americans for Contraception and Girl Effect, which works with adolescent girls through media and community programmes.Preventing gender-based violenceSix organisations were selected to strengthen efforts to prevent violence against women and girls, support survivors and challenge harmful social norms. Their work includes community programmes, advocacy and efforts to improve protections for those at risk.Named recipients include Ujamaa Africa, which works to prevent gender-based violence through programmes in African communities, and Serenas, an organisation working in this field.Why the grants are unrestrictedA central feature of the Women's Health Co-Lab is its use of unrestricted funding. Instead of requiring recipients to spend every dollar on a narrowly defined activity, the initiative allows organisations greater flexibility to decide how the money can best support their work.This approach is intended to reduce administrative burdens and help organisations respond to changing circumstances. A group working on maternal health may need to strengthen healthcare delivery, while an organisation focused on violence prevention may prioritise community education, survivor support or policy advocacy.Co-Impact worked with recipients to refine their plans and budgets as part of the grantmaking process. The collaborative approach gives organisations a role in determining how the funding can best advance their objectives.Ujamaa Africa receives $3 millionUjamaa Africa was among the organisations selected for funding, receiving an unrestricted grant of $3 million. The organisation works to prevent gender-based violence through programmes that engage young people and communities.Its executive director, Benjamin Omondi Mboya, said the funding would help the organisation expand its programmes across Kenya, Malawi and Somaliland.The grant illustrates how flexible funding can help organisations adapt their programmes to local needs rather than relying entirely on short-term, tightly restricted project grants.Who else is backing the initiative?The founding donor group included Tricia Black and Patrick Brogan, Marie Dageville, Rachel Markham and Cedric Dageville, Holly Fogle and Jeff Lieberman, Barrie Glabman and Adam Schwartz, Susan Long Hall and C. David Hall, Renee and Alexis Lê-Quôc, Aarti Lohia, Diksha and Divesh Makan, Samantha McManus and David Karp, Andrea Meditch, Rick and Nancy Moskovitz, Susan and Erin Samueli, and the Tullman family.ICONIQ Impact helped bring the donors together, while Co-Impact contributed experience in supporting organisations working to strengthen health, education and economic systems. Their partnership reflects an approach in which multiple donors pool resources around shared priorities.Why women's health and safety are a priorityWomen's health outcomes are influenced by more than access to medical treatment. Maternal care, reproductive health services and protection from violence are also shaped by healthcare infrastructure, public policy, social attitudes and economic circumstances.Organisations working in these areas often require sustained support to train healthcare workers, provide services, advocate for policy changes and reach underserved communities. The Co-Lab's three-year funding model is intended to give recipients greater scope to plan and expand their work.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Why is Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to PM Modi?': Abhijeet Dipke on Delhi police assaults
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday accused Delhi Police of assaulting protesters, journalists and even MPs amid the
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday accused Delhi Police of assaulting protesters, journalists and even MPs amid the crackdown on demonstrations demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation.Questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s support for the CEC, Dipke alleged that the scale of police action showed the government was prepared to use force to protect Kumar.In a post on X, Dipke questioned why the authorities were taking such measures against people protesting over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls."Youth are being assaulted, journalists are being assaulted even MPs are being assaulted by Delhi Police."He added, "What makes Gyanesh Kumar so indispensable to PM Modi that he is willing to wage war against everyone just to protect him?"CJP alleges assault on protesters during Delhi crackdownDipke’s remarks came after CJP called for a demonstration against Kumar at Jantar Mantar, which was prevented from taking place amid extensive security deployment and preventive detentions across the capital.The party has alleged that police personnel used force against its supporters during the protests. CJP had also claimed that its Mumbai lead, Pranay Ahire, was brutally assaulted during the demonstration and was receiving treatment at a hospital.CPM MP John Brittas alleges assault by Delhi PoliceThe controversy has also extended to opposition leaders. CPM Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas wrote to the Chief Justice of India, President Droupadi Murmu and Rajya Sabha chairman CP Radhakrishnan, alleging that Delhi Police personnel dragged him away, lifted him and assaulted him inside a police vehicle while he was interacting with journalists during the protests.Brittas sought an independent investigation and accountability, alleging that the incident raised questions about parliamentary privilege and the right to peaceful expression.CJP vows to continue campaign against CECThe CJP has maintained that its campaign will continue until Kumar resigns. The party’s demands include action over alleged electoral-roll irregularities and the scrapping of the SIR exercise.The protests have triggered a wider political confrontation, with opposition leaders questioning the police response and authorities citing law-and-order concerns behind the security measures.(With agency inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Delhi | Silver Rate in Delhi | Bank Holidays in Delhi | Public Holidays in Delhi | Delhi AQI | Weather in Delhi | Petrol Price in Delhi | Diesel Price in Delhi | CNG Price in Delhi | LPG Price in DelhiStay updated with the latest Delhi news. articles.summary: A woman rejected a man after going on a flamboyant date at a Michelin-star restaurant, and the man’s reaction to the message has sparked a debate around
articles.body: A woman rejected a man after going on a flamboyant date at a Michelin-star restaurant, and the man’s reaction to the message has sparked a debate around chivalry on social media.According to screenshots shared on X, a woman told her date she didn’t see a future with him after an expensive first outing. In his response, he asked her to return the $1,050 (about Rs 1 lakh) he had spent on the evening.Dating has always come with unwritten rules. Who pays on dates? Who texts first? How much is too much on a first meeting? There is no particular rulebook for it, so most of us learn with experience over time, error, and the occasional awkward silence at the end of the night.Let’s dig in to find out what exactly happened when the man’s response took an unexpected turn.Woman rejects a man after date at a Michelin star restaurant, man’s response brings him under a controversyA woman's rejection after an expensive first date has sparked a debate on X. According to the post she shared on her account, the man she had dated asked her to return $1,050 or nearly Rs 1 lakh, which was the cost of their date at the luxurious restaurant. The screenshots were posted by X user Raq (@raqisright), who appears to be the woman involved. She captioned the post as "Chivalry is dead."The debate picked up traction when she hared the reason why she had rejected himShe reshared an earlier post where she had described how they spent the evening and how the man had made her feel special, explaining that she wrote, “ Went on a first date last night. He kept it a surprise and called me a black car to the restaurant - a michelin star. He opened the doors and told me to turn my brain off and ordered everything all night. I felt so protected and secured. And then I friend-zoned him because he’s bald and like be so for real rn.”Social media responseThe internet had a mixed response, while some criticised the man for asking for money back after being turned down. Others thought spending so much on a first date was unnecessary. One user wrote, “"But to be honest, a Michelin-star restaurant for a first date was a risky move. Coffee would've achieved the same results and cost $20."Another user supporting the man wrote, "Absolutely warranted. So many women out in the world just want men to have them pay for a lavish lifestyle with no commitment. There are so many great men out in the world who are still single because they are avoiding women who just want to take instead of giving back." Another group argued that if a man chooses to pay, it shouldn't automatically become a debt just because the relationship didn't work out.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: In 1992, Tyler Perry put his $12,000 savings into a failed Atlanta play and later spent months living in a car; decades later his $750,000 gift helped pay back taxes for 300+ seniors and freeze taxes for 100 more
articles.summary: Tyler Perry, renowned filmmaker and actor, has made a significant donation of $750,000 to assist low-income senior citizens in Atlanta with their property taxes, helping them stay in their homes. This initiative addresses rising property tax pressures faced by elderly residents on fixed incomes.
articles.body: Tyler Perry, who once spent three months living in his car after losing $12,000 on a failed theatre production, has donated $750,000 to help low-income senior citizens in Atlanta pay property taxes and remain in their homes.Perry is an American filmmaker, actor, director, producer and writer, best known for creating the Madea character and building a career across theatre, film and television.He started out writing and performing stage plays in the 1990s before expanding into screen productions. His work includes more than 1,200 television episodes, 22 feature films and numerous stage plays.Perry founded Tyler Perry Studios in Atlanta, where he continues to produce film and television content. According to Forbes, his fortune is estimated at $1.4.The contribution will cover outstanding property taxes for more than 300 low-income seniors and help another 100 avoid future increases through a pilot programme.Rising property taxes have put pressure on older residents living on fixed incomes, making it harder for some to remain in homes they have occupied for years. Perry’s donation will cover outstanding city, county and school property taxes, with the funds administered by Invest Atlanta Partnership, the nonprofit arm of the city’s economic development authority.How the donation will help Atlanta seniorsThe $750,000 contribution has two main purposes. The first is to clear overdue property taxes for more than 300 low-income senior residents in Atlanta. The assistance will cover taxes owed to the city, county and school authorities.The second part will support a pilot programme for 100 low-income seniors, using funds to cover the difference between their current property taxes and any increases. The aim is to help them manage rising costs and remain in their homes.“Atlanta’s growth and prosperity should not come at the expense of our legacy residents, many of whom have been priced out of their homes in previous years,” Mayor Dickens said.“Tyler Perry has been engaged in our ongoing conversations around legacy resident retention, and he told me he wanted to do something to support these efforts. Thanks to his generosity, more Atlantans will be able to remain in the communities they built.”From a failed play to a billion-dollar fortunePerry began his career in live theatre in the 1990s. He put $12,000 of his savings into producing I Know I’ve Been Changed, a play about survivors of child abuse, at a community theatre in Atlanta.The production initially failed to attract a large enough paying audience to cover his expenses. Perry struggled to pay rent and spent three months living in his car on and off while revising the show and trying to build an audience. He handled several aspects of the production himself, including designing the set, preparing programmes, hanging lights and selling snacks during intermissions.He continued touring his plays, gradually building a following before moving into film and television. His Madea franchise has grossed more than $660 million, as per the Forbes.Perry’s business model has also centred on retaining ownership of his work. In 2019, he opened Tyler Perry Studios, a 330-acre production complex in Atlanta. That year, he also struck a deal with Viacom that gave him a 25% stake in streaming service BET+.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: The Poetry Of Petroleum?
articles.summary: Oil is the new oil. The events of the last few months have confirmed the criticality of fuel.
articles.body: Oil is the new oil. The events of the last few months have confirmed the criticality of fuel. But beyond the geopolitics of oil lurks an intriguing question: what exactly is fuel?Why do some things carry within them energy that can be released while other material show no such properties? For here is something utterly astonishing about a litre of petrol. Not because of its utility. The astonishing thing about petrol is that it transports an event that happened millions of years ago intact to our roads. It is a liquid like many others, yet capable of hurling five tonnes of metal down a highway.When you turn the key in your car, ancient sunlight is activated. Poetry aside, that is the truth. What we call oil is the energy of sunlight trapped in biological matter. Over geological time, that sunlight was transformed, compressed and preserved. And we get to use that today in our everyday lives. The energy of the Sun is the source of almost all fuels that have sustained civilisation. Coal and oil preserve its ancient light. Wind and rivers are its continuing work.Uranium is an important exception to this pattern. It is not a product of sunlight, nor of any form of life. Its past is more glorious—it precedes even the sun, back to a time of violent cosmic events that took place before our solar system even existed. When we split an atom of uranium, what we are releasing is not a product of life, but something that existed long before life itself.All fuels seem to share one property—their energy needs to be released before it becomes useful. It needs to be actively harnessed; without that intervention, it just expends the energy ever so gradually, so as to escape notice.In a sense then, the log was burning well before it was set on fire. Only the process was too slow to be visible. The log would be left to rot itself over large periods of time. What we call rotting is in fact another kind of fire. And not just a log—a nail that rusts in the rain goes through the same transformation. A fire is more theatrical—its intention is more hungry and obvious, but in some senses the rusting, rotting, decaying are just the names we give slower, milder forms of fire. The gentleness of the vocabulary used is misleading, for the difference lies not in the journey but in the speed of travel.But the nail is not fuel in spite of the fact that it releases minute quantities of energy over time. The energy it leaks out slowly from the metal and vanishes into the ether, much like how a whisper is lost in a crowded room. What makes rust rust and petrol petrol is that the latter releases energy fast enough for us to use it.What makes fuel special is its ability to keep a form of the past alive in the present. It hoards energy, keeping it intact until it can be released with speed. Unlike a fossil, which is also a record of the past, fuel is inert but alive. A fossil is the past made perfect, fuel is the present made continuous. Fuel is history in three dimensions, the past still capable of action rather than merely of being remembered.Fossil fuel accumulates over geological time but expends itself in biological time. In nothing else, does so much time get extinguished so quickly. Fuel is the most barbaric consumption of time that we can see. Human beings are the voracious beasts that treat millennia with casual contempt, using up millions of years of heat and pressure to move a few kilometres.The same is true of a grain of wheat. Like petrol, it stores sunlight that is meant to power the next generation of the crop. We rob this energy for our own purposes. A grain of wheat and a litre of petrol have more in common than is obvious. Both carry the consequences of a past event in a form that remains available for future use, provided something comes along that can harness it.These objects have the rare ability to refuse to die easily. Fuel has a reservoir of life within it, one that gives it a robust afterlife. Seeds give birth to the next generation. DNA passes on traits. Food transfers sunlight from this generation to the next.A feature of all forms of life is that they are driven to carry the past forward. Life is hardwired to produce life. Human beings, in particular, have evolved many ways, beyond biology, of storing the past for the use of the future. Writing stores thought and brings the collected wisdom of the past for the use of the future.Money is a store of labour which makes exchange possible. What we call civilisation could reasonably be seen as a way of making the present continuous with the past, of ensuring that a new generation does not begin from zero all over again. The past is not over. We are testimony to that. Not only do we come from the past, but we consume it in prodigious quantities to keep us going. As if there were no tomorrow.

articles.title: No more a free circus, but a tamasha worth crores
articles.summary: The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed several serious
articles.body: The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed several serious questions before the country’s political culture and democratic system. Congress and left-wing organizations have demanded the immediate removal of Gyanesh Kumar from the post of Chief Election Commissioner.A petition regarding this had also been filed in the Supreme Court. This petition demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar from his post. Even after the Supreme Court dismissed this petition, Congress’ Yuvraj Rahul Gandhi, along with his party’s MPs, has been wreaking havoc on the streets of Delhi every single day.There is a popular saying in Maharashtra, “Bin Paishacha Tamasha”, which means a tamasha born out of sheer foolishness that costs not even a penny. This surely entertains the onlookers. But the tamasha of the protest staged by the Congress and left-wing organizations is not free of cost; instead, it is costing crores of rupees every day. Paid protesters are being brought in. Unmasking the mastermind behind this multi-crore drama deserves a separate article.There is a competition going on between Rahul Gandhi and left-wing student unions to prove who is better in expressing fierce opposition to the Modi government by taking to the streets. When the footage of a young woman representing left-wing organizations climbing over a barricade and pushing women police officers went viral on social media, Yuvraj Gandhi felt a sudden urge to show just how brave he was. He began to fear that his own TRP might drop when this young woman was systematically brought into the limelight by left-wing organizations.It was out of this fear that he staged a protest march to the Chief Election Commissioner's office and satisfied his urge by climbing over police barricades. No country in the world has ever seen an opposition leader so childish, shallow and terrified for his very existence. Rahul Gandhi has sworn to tarnish the reputation of the office of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.He takes pride in bringing each and every Lok Sabha session to a standstill by creating a ruckus. Even though the Delhi Police have denied permission for the protest, Rahul Gandhi has become an expert at things like pushing down the police barricades and manhandling police officers. He is making a desperate attempt to prove himself as the Leader of the Opposition by acting like a Bollywood hero. He has destroyed his own reputation due to this frenzied behaviour.Rahul Gandhi does not have the intellectual capacity to understand that such cheap aggression does not help in politics. He should learn how to oppose a government from his grandmother Mrs. Indira Gandhi's life. The Janata Party government had appointed the Shah Commission to inquire into the atrocities committed during the Emergency.The Shah Commission found Indira Gandhi guilty. Subsequently, the police went to her home to arrest her. Mrs. Indira Gandhi surrendered to the police without any ruckus. But before that, she had called all the journalists and photographers in Delhi to her home. She calmly got herself arrested in front of them. She systematically gained the sympathy of voters through this. Now, that is what you call a shrewd politician.These days, Rahul Gandhi keeps on picking fights with the police over one thing or the other. His tactics, like marching towards the Prime Minister’s residence or attempting to enter the Election Commission’s office, show that he does not have even a basic understanding of politics. Even the common man has started to realise that Rahul Gandhi was just trying to get some publicity by trying to enter the Election Commission’s office without any prior appointment. Rahul Gandhi has decided to defy all parliamentary and government rules, conventions and laws.From a security perspective, security rules are extremely strict at places in Delhi such as Parliament House, Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Prime Minister’s residence etc. Rahul Gandhi must certainly be aware of the laws and rules, as he has been an MP for more than 22 years. Still, he is trying to break the law again and again. He is still not mature enough to understand that such gimmicks give temporary publicity, but do not make his leadership popular. In fact, it seems that he does not even want to develop such maturity.Not a single Congress leader currently has the courage to tell Rahul Gandhi, who has been criticizing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), that the Congress won in Kerala after this exercise was carried out. Rahul Gandhi, who accuses the EVMs of being manipulated, deliberately ignores the fact that he himself won an election by a margin of more than six lakh votes which was conducted using these very EVMs. He also conveniently forgets that the BJP won a majority when election was conducted through EVMs in 2014, when his own party was in power.Yuvraj is even failing to understand that such behaviour is causing him to lose his standing among the people. He is so obsessed with publicity that he has even forgotten that he is fighting against Narendra Modi and the Bharatiya Janata Party. He thinks that he is in competition with the youth who are gaining publicity by protesting in Delhi. He is not even bothered that he is adding to the difficulties faced by ordinary people in the Delhi region by staging protests every now and then and blocking roads. These protests can, at most, make him a reel star for a few days. He won’t get anything beyond that. Of course, he does not have the intellectual capacity to understand this. Therefore, there is no doubt that he will be more provocative and dramatic in the coming days.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
